This file concatenates README.md, AGENTS.md and every guide in docs/ (generated by
scripts/gen_docs.py). The API, types and coverage references are separate files listed in
llms.txt.

<!-- file: README.md -->

# ultrarouter Python SDK

[![Python 3.10 to 3.14](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%20to%203.14-blue.svg)](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/pyproject.toml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/LICENSE)

The official Python client for ultrarouter, an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway with model routing,
fallbacks, evals, and an outcome ledger that records what happened after a model answered.

- **OpenAI-compatible**: `client.chat.completions.create(...)`, `client.embeddings.create(...)`,
  `client.models.list()`, streaming, tools and structured outputs, or hand an existing
  `openai` client the gateway with `client.as_openai()`.
- **Sync and async**: `UltraRouter` and `AsyncUltraRouter` have the same surface.
- **Typed**: every response is a pydantic v2 model; the package ships `py.typed` and passes
  `mypy --strict`.
- **Production defaults**: a total time budget per call, automatic retries with backoff for
  transient failures, idempotency keys on every write, and typed errors.
- **Plug-and-play learning**: correlate requests and multi-step episodes, report whether a task
  succeeded (`client.outcomes.report`) the moment you know, with durable receipts and no double
  counting, steer learning per call type (`client.learning`), and turn verifiers, business rules
  and signed webhooks into verdicts (`ultrarouter.adapters`).
- **Beyond chat**: call types, hosted prompts, Bench comparisons, outcomes, preflight with
  learned context, a reviewer adapter, and a pure context runtime (`ultrarouter.context`).

> Status: `0.1.0` is an early (alpha) release. The API surface may change before `1.0`.
> You need an ultrarouter API key and the URL of a gateway you have access to.

## Install

The package is **not on PyPI** (or any registry) yet, so `pip install ultrarouter` does not work.
Build a wheel from this repository and install it, or install from the GitHub source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python.git
cd ultrarouter-sdk-python && uv build
pip install dist/ultrarouter-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl            # add [openai] for client.as_openai()

# or, without cloning:
pip install "ultrarouter @ git+https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python.git"
```

Python 3.10 or newer. Runtime dependencies: `httpx`, `pydantic` (v2) and `typing-extensions`. See
[Installation](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/installation.md).

## 60-second quickstart

Set your key and the URL of the gateway you have access to (there is no default gateway):

```bash
export ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY="ur_sk_test_..."
export ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL="https://gateway.example.com"   # or http://localhost:8080 for a local gateway
```

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()  # reads ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY and ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL

reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a one-line greeting."}],
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)
print(reply.ur.request_id, reply.ur.model_served, reply.ur.cost_usd)
```

Every response carries an `ur` block: the request id (use it for feedback and stats), the model
that actually served the call, the provider, the routing decision and the cost in USD.

The async client is the same API with `await`:

```python
import asyncio

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncUltraRouter() as client:
        reply = await client.chat.completions.create(
            model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a one-line greeting."}],
        )
        print(reply.choices[0].message.content)


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Configuration

| Setting | Constructor argument | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `api_key=` | `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY` (or `UR_API_KEY`) | required |
| Gateway URL | `base_url=` | `ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL` (or `UR_BASE_URL`) | required |
| Default model | `default_model=` | | none |
| Time budget per call | `timeout=` (seconds) | | `600` |
| Automatic retries | `max_retries=` | | `2` |
| Extra headers | `default_headers=` | | none |

Point `base_url` at any deployment (self-hosted, staging, a local stack); a trailing `/v1` is
accepted. See [Configuration](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) for per-call defaults (`defaults=`), the
`autopilot` routing intent and Bench tagging.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter(
    base_url="https://gateway.example.com",
    default_model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    defaults={"call_type": "support-reply", "max_cost_usd": 0.05},
    timeout=60,
    max_retries=3,
)
reply = client.chat.completions.create(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])
print(reply.ur.model_served)
```

## Feature tour

**Streaming.** `stream=True` returns an iterator of chunks; the last chunk carries usage and
the `ur` block, also available on the stream afterwards.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
with client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Count to three."}],
    stream=True,
) as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        if chunk.choices and chunk.choices[0].delta.content:
            print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content, end="", flush=True)
print()
print(stream.ur.request_id if stream.ur else None)
```

**Embeddings and models.**

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
vectors = client.embeddings.create(model="openai/text-embedding-3-small", input=["alpha", "beta"])
print(len(vectors.data), len(vectors.data[0].embedding))

for model in client.models.list(provider="openai").data:
    print(model.id, model.pricing.input_usd_per_1m)
```

**Feedback and post-hoc stats** for a served request:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}]
)
client.requests.feedback(reply.ur.request_id, rating=1, tags=["helpful"])
stats = client.generation.get(reply.ur.request_id)
print(stats.tokens.total, stats.cost.total_usd)
```

**Outcomes**: record what happened after the answer (accepted, edited, resolved) on an
*artifact*, durably queued and retried without double counting:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
with client.with_artifact("ticket:4812:reply") as scope:
    draft = scope.chat.completions.create(
        model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Draft a reply about a late order."}],
    )
    scope.record({"channel": "behavioral", "kind": "accepted"})
```

**Plug-and-play learning**: report whether the task succeeded, right after the answer (the gateway
accepts it as `pending` with a durable receipt if it has not stored the request yet), from a named
source: `verifier`, `business_rule`, `webhook` and `human_review` teach; `self_rating` only ranks;
`unknown` sends nothing. Reporting twice never counts twice.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
with client.episode("order:A-100") as episode:  # every step carries the episode key
    reply = episode.chat.completions.create(
        model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Process order A-100."}],
    )
    report = episode.report("pass", source="verifier")  # on the last step
print(report.outcome_status, report.teaches)  # "pending" True
final = client.outcomes.wait_for_receipt(report)  # bounded polling of the public receipt
print(final.status)  # "applied"
```

See [Plug-and-play learning](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/learning.md)
for correlation with the `openai` package, receipts, outcome adapters, learning controls and the
demonstration environment.

More: [call types and hosted prompts](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/call-types.md), [Bench](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/bench.md),
[preflight and learned context](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/preflight.md), [the reviewer adapter](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/reviewer.md),
[the context runtime](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/context-runtime.md) and the [full guide index](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/index.md).

## Use it as the OpenAI client

Already using the `openai` package? Keep your code and point it at the gateway:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

openai_client = UltraRouter().as_openai()  # an openai.OpenAI configured for the gateway
reply = openai_client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}]
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)
```

`AsyncUltraRouter().as_openai()` returns an `openai.AsyncOpenAI`. See
[OpenAI compatibility](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/openai-compatibility.md).

For the OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages APIs, point the official `openai` and `anthropic`
SDKs straight at the gateway by changing only the base URL and the key; the gateway forwards the
body verbatim and meters the call. See
[Native passthrough](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/passthrough.md).

## Errors and retries

Failures raise typed exceptions that all derive from `UltraRouterError` and carry `code`,
`status`, `message`, `request_id` and `retryable`:

```python
from ultrarouter import ModelUnpricedError, RateLimitError, UltraRouter, UltraRouterError

client = UltraRouter()
try:
    client.chat.completions.create(
        model="acme/unpriced-model", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}]
    )
except ModelUnpricedError as exc:  # 403: the gateway will not call a model it cannot price
    print("pick a priced model:", exc.message)
except RateLimitError:
    print("still rate limited after automatic retries")
except UltraRouterError as exc:
    print(exc.code, exc.status, exc.request_id)
```

The SDK retries connection errors and 408/429/5xx responses that the gateway did not mark
`retryable: false` (two retries by default, jittered exponential backoff, `Retry-After`
honoured), all within the call's total `timeout`. Every non-streaming `POST` carries an
`Idempotency-Key` that stays the same across retries. Streams are not retried. Details:
[Errors](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/errors.md) and [Retries, timeouts and idempotency](https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python/blob/main/docs/retries-timeouts.md).

  endpoint the SDK calls, sync and async).

<!-- file: AGENTS.md -->

# AGENTS.md: using and changing the ultrarouter Python SDK

This file is for AI coding agents (and humans in a hurry). Part 1 is for agents writing code that
**uses** the SDK; part 2 is for agents **changing** this repository.

## Part 1: using the SDK

### Install

`ultrarouter` is **not on PyPI** (or any registry) yet: `pip install ultrarouter` fails. Install a
wheel built from the repository, or the GitHub source:

```bash
uv build && pip install dist/ultrarouter-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl   # "...whl[openai]" for as_openai()
pip install "ultrarouter @ git+https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python.git"
```

Python 3.10+. Import name: `ultrarouter`. Never tell a user `pip install ultrarouter` works.

### Configure from the environment

Never hardcode keys. The client reads `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY` and `ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL`:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()  # create once, reuse; close with client.close() or use `with`
```

### Canonical patterns

```python
from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter, UltraRouter, UltraRouterError

client = UltraRouter(default_model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini")

# Chat
reply = client.chat.completions.create(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])
text = reply.choices[0].message.content
request_id = reply.ur.request_id  # keep it: feedback, stats and support use it

# Streaming
with client.chat.completions.create(
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}], stream=True
) as stream:
    streamed = stream.text()

# Embeddings
vectors = client.embeddings.create(model="openai/text-embedding-3-small", input=["a", "b"])

# Errors: catch the base class, branch on subclasses or .code
try:
    client.chat.completions.create(
        model="acme/unpriced-model", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}]
    )
except UltraRouterError as exc:
    print(exc.code, exc.status, exc.retryable, exc.request_id)

# Outcomes: what happened after the answer (durably queued, never raises on delivery failure)
receipt = client.outcomes.record(
    {"request": request_id}, {"channel": "behavioral", "kind": "accepted"}
)
client.outcomes.flush()

# Learning loop: correlate, then report whether the task succeeded (see docs/learning.md)
with client.episode("order:A-100") as episode:  # key -> X-UR-Artifact; ids minted per step
    episode.chat.completions.create(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Process A-100"}])
    report = episode.report("pass", source="verifier")  # pass | fail | unknown
if report.reported and report.receipt_id:
    final = client.outcomes.wait_for_receipt(report)  # pending -> applied
call_type = next((ct for ct in client.call_types.list().data if ct.slug == "support-reply"), None)
if call_type is None:
    call_type = client.call_types.create(slug="support-reply")
status = client.learning.status(call_type.id)  # learning requires the ct_… id, not the slug
```

Async: `AsyncUltraRouter` has the same methods; `await` them and use `async with`.

### Pitfalls

- **Model ids are provider-prefixed**: `openai/gpt-5.2-mini`, not `gpt-5.2-mini`. List them with
  `client.models.list()`.
- **One client per process**, not per request; it owns a connection pool.
- **Do not retry what the SDK already retried.** It retries 408/429/5xx (unless the gateway says
  `retryable: false`) and connection errors, within the total `timeout`. `ModelUnpricedError`
  (`model_unpriced`, 403) and other 4xx are never retried: change the request instead.
- **Streams are not retried** and have no idempotency key.
- **`bench.run(wait=True)` returns `BenchRunTrigger | BenchRun`**: narrow with
  `isinstance(run, BenchRun)` before using `run.id`.
- **Preflight for case-based modules needs `messages=`**; otherwise `knowledge` is `None` with
  `knowledge_reason == "case_query_missing"`.
- **Outcome events and reviewer events never contain prompt or completion text.** Without
  corrections consent, report edits with `ultrarouter.diff_stats(draft, final)`.
- **Bench capture is for test keys** (`ur_sk_test_...`).
- **Unknown response fields are kept** in `model.model_extra`; do not assume a field is absent
  because the model class lacks it.
- **Enumerated response fields are `str`**, so compare against string literals.
- **Do not log the client's key** (`client.api_key`) or request/response bodies.
- **Report outcomes with `client.outcomes.report(request_id, verdict, source=...)`**; never sleep
  before reporting (an early report is held as `pending` with a durable receipt). `unknown`
  sends nothing; `self_rating` never teaches; HTTP or tool success is not task success.
- **Concurrent episodes need distinct `episode_key`s**: without one the gateway groups steps by
  their opening text, so identical concurrent tasks would merge.
- **A report is idempotent by identity** (`request_id`, `verdict`, `source`, `idempotency_key`):
  repeats replay the same event; give two genuinely different verdicts different
  `idempotency_key`s, and pass `observed_at` when a report may be repeated from another process.
- **Learning controls return a `LearningControl`**; the status is `control.learning`. A refusal
  is a `LearningError` subclass: branch on `reason`, show `action`.
- **Learning needs the full workspace self-learning opt-in** (knowledge and corrections consent).
  An owner/admin grants it on the dashboard Learning page or through the signed-in session
  `PUT /v1/workspaces/{id}/self-learning` with `{"enabled":true}`. An API key cannot grant consent;
  corrections consent alone is insufficient.
- **`ultrarouter.demo` is a demonstration**, not evidence that learning improves an agent.

### Where to look

| Need | Location |

| Runnable scripts | [examples/](examples/) (`learning_*.py` for the learning loop) |
| The learning loop | [docs/learning.md](docs/learning.md) |
| All docs in one file for an LLM | [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) (index: [llms.txt](llms.txt)) |

## Part 2: changing this repository

### Setup and commands

```bash
uv sync                      # creates .venv with dev dependencies
make check                   # the full gate: lint, format, types, tests, docs, build, smoke, leak scan
make test                    # pytest only
make lint format typecheck   # individual gates
make generate                # regenerate types, API/types reference, coverage table, llms files
make smoke                   # build wheel + sdist, install into fresh 3.10 and 3.14 venvs, exercise them
make test-lowest             # the suite with httpx, pydantic, typing-extensions and openai at their floors
make leak-scan               # scan the tree, git history and dist/ for secrets (+ $ULTRAROUTER_LEAK_PATTERNS_FILE)
make parity-check            # regenerate the parity goldens from the TypeScript SDK and diff (TS_SDK=path)
```

The `ci` workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, manual dispatch only; `make check` is the gate) runs the
same gates on Python 3.10 to 3.14; `publish.yml` uploads to PyPI with trusted publishing, only from a
published release or a manual run.

### Rules

- `openapi/openapi.yaml` is a synced artifact: update it only with
  `python scripts/sync_openapi.py --from <spec>`, then `make generate`.
- `src/ultrarouter/types/_generated.py` is generated by `scripts/gen_types.py`; never edit it.
  Change names in the tables at the top of the generator.
- Every public module, class, function and method needs a docstring (a test enforces it).
- Every ```` ```python ```` block in `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `docs/*.md` is executed against
  the mock gateway by `tests/test_docs.py`. Keep examples runnable.
- `docs/api-reference.md`, `docs/types-reference.md`, `docs/api-coverage.md`, `llms.txt` and
  `llms-full.txt` are generated; tests fail when they drift.
- Every API-key endpoint in the spec must be mapped in `tests/coverage_map.py` (or explicitly
  excluded with a reason); `tests/test_api_coverage.py` calls each one sync and async and validates
  the request body against the spec.
- `src/ultrarouter/_data/outcome_verdicts.json` and `_data/toy_env.json` are byte-for-byte copies
  of fixtures shared with the TypeScript SDK (also under `tests/fixtures/`, sha256 pinned in
  `tests/test_outcome_report.py` and `tests/test_demo.py`). Never edit them here.
- After a spec sync adds operations, run `make generate`, give new response and request models
  public names in the tables at the top of `scripts/gen_types.py`, and map each new API-key
  operation in `tests/coverage_map.py`.
- Cross-language behaviour (context runtime, placement, rendering, diff stats, canonical JSON) is
  pinned by `tests/fixtures/parity/`; regenerate with
  `node scripts/gen_parity_goldens.mjs --ts-sdk <path to the TypeScript SDK>`.
- `mypy --strict` and `ruff` must stay clean. No new runtime dependencies without a strong reason.
- Run `make leak-scan` before committing. Never add organisation-specific patterns or names to
  this repository (not even in tests); they belong in the private patterns file the scanner
  reads from `ULTRAROUTER_LEAK_PATTERNS_FILE`. Test the scanner with synthetic patterns.

### Layout

```
src/ultrarouter/          the package (clients, transport, resources, helpers)
  types/_generated.py     generated models and request shapes
  _data/                  shared fixtures shipped in the package (verdict mapping, toy environment)
  adapters/               outcome adapters (verifiers, business rules, signed webhooks)
  demo/                   the deterministic demonstration environment
  context/                the pure context runtime
tests/                    unit, coverage, parity, docs and example tests; support/ has the mock gateway
docs/                     guides (tested) and generated references
examples/                 runnable scripts (tested)
scripts/                  generators, leak scan, smoke test
openapi/openapi.yaml      the synced API specification
```

# ultrarouter Python SDK documentation

The `ultrarouter` package is the Python client for the ultrarouter gateway. Start with
[Installation](installation.md) and the [quickstart in the README](../README.md), then use the
guides below. Every Python example in these pages is executed by the test suite against a local
mock gateway, so the snippets match the code.

## Getting started

| Guide | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Installation](installation.md) | from a locally built wheel or the GitHub source (not on PyPI yet); the `openai` extra; supported Python versions |
| [Configuration and authentication](configuration.md) | API keys, base URL and self-hosted gateways, environment variables, client defaults, `autopilot`, Bench tagging |
| [Sync and async clients](clients.md) | `UltraRouter` vs `AsyncUltraRouter`, lifecycle, connection pools, `with_options`, concurrency |

## OpenAI-compatible surface

| Guide | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Chat completions](chat-completions.md) | `client.chat.completions.create`, parameters, the `ur` response block |
| [Streaming](streaming.md) | `stream=True`, `Stream` / `AsyncStream`, final usage and `ur` |
| [Tools](tools.md) | function calling, tool results, streaming tool-call fragments |
| [Structured outputs](structured-outputs.md) | `response_format` with JSON schema, parsing into pydantic |
| [Embeddings](embeddings.md) | `client.embeddings.create`, float and base64 encodings |
| [Models and key info](models.md) | `client.models.list`, `client.models.retrieve`, `client.key.get` |
| [OpenAI compatibility](openai-compatibility.md) | `as_openai()`, migrating from the `openai` package |
| [Native passthrough](passthrough.md) | the official `openai` and `anthropic` SDKs through the gateway: `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, the ur metering headers |

## ultrarouter surfaces

| Guide | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Call types](call-types.md) | create, configure and evaluate call types; recommendations |
| [Hosted prompts](hosted-prompts.md) | versioned prompts, activation and rollback, `get_prompt` |
| [Prompt rendering](prompt-render.md) | `render_prompt` and `render_hosted_prompt_result` |
| [Verified memory](verified-memory.md) | enable, inspect and disable answering from verified cases |
| [Feedback](feedback.md) | thumbs up / down on a served request |
| [Generation lookup](generation.md) | tokens, cost, timing and routing for one request |
| [Autopilot](autopilot.md) | the routing intent and the readiness report |
| [Bench](bench.md) | capture, freeze, paired runs, reports and the compare gate |
| [Outcomes and artifacts](outcomes.md) | artifact types, artifacts, outcome events, finals, the durable queue |
| [Plug-and-play learning](learning.md) | request and episode correlation, verdict reports with receipts, outcome adapters, learning controls, the demonstration environment |
| [History imports](imports.md) | import usage exports or traces without proxying |
| [Flywheel](flywheel.md) | status, exposure grants, candidates, confirmations, plans, improvement reads |
| [Oracles and verdict sources](oracles.md) | register and qualify your own checks; source checks |
| [Reviewer adapter](reviewer.md) | signed human decisions, dead letters and repair |
| [Preflight and learned context](preflight.md) | `preflight`, `use_learned`, `messages` for case modules, caching |

| [Diff statistics](diff-stats.md) | `diff_stats` for reporting edits without sending text |
| [Context runtime](context-runtime.md) | `ultrarouter.context`: lift, compile, render, exit |

<!-- file: docs/installation.md -->

# Installation

The package is named `ultrarouter` and supports Python 3.10 through 3.14.

> **Not on PyPI yet.** `pip install ultrarouter` does not work today: the package has not been
> published to any package registry. Install it from a wheel you build from the repository, or
> straight from the public GitHub source.

## From a locally built wheel

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python.git
cd ultrarouter-sdk-python
uv build                                    # writes dist/ultrarouter-<version>-py3-none-any.whl and the sdist
pip install dist/ultrarouter-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

Copy the wheel wherever you need it; it has no build-time requirements. With uv or Poetry, add the
file path the same way (`uv add ./dist/ultrarouter-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`,
`poetry add ./dist/ultrarouter-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`).

## From the GitHub source

```bash
pip install "ultrarouter @ git+https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python.git"
uv add "ultrarouter @ git+https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python.git"
```

Pin a commit for reproducible installs (`...ultrarouter-sdk-python.git@<commit>`).

## The `openai` extra

`client.as_openai()` returns an `openai.OpenAI` (or `openai.AsyncOpenAI`) preconfigured for the
gateway. It needs the `openai` package, which the extra installs:

```bash
pip install "dist/ultrarouter-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl[openai]"
pip install "ultrarouter[openai] @ git+https://github.com/lucastonon/ultrarouter-sdk-python.git"
```

Or install `openai` yourself (`pip install "openai>=1.55.3"`). Without it, `as_openai()` raises an
`UltraRouterError` with code `dependency_missing` explaining what to install. Everything else works
without it. The extra requires `openai>=1.55.3`: older `openai` releases cannot construct a client
with `httpx` 0.28 or newer.

## Dependencies

| Package | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `httpx` (>=0.27, <1) | HTTP transport, connection pooling, sync and async |
| `pydantic` (>=2.7, <3) | typed response models |
| `typing-extensions` (>=4.12) | `TypedDict`, `Required` and `Unpack` on Python 3.10 |
| `openai` (>=1.55.3, optional) | `as_openai()` |

Every lower bound is tested: the suite runs with all dependencies at their floors, and with each
of `httpx`, `pydantic` and `openai` at its floor while the others are at their newest versions
(`make test-lowest`).

The context runtime (`ultrarouter.context`), the outcome adapters (`ultrarouter.adapters`), the
demonstration environment (`ultrarouter.demo`) and the pure helpers (`diff_stats`,
`render_prompt`, learned placement) use only the standard library and pydantic.

## Verify the installation

```python
import ultrarouter

print(ultrarouter.__version__)
```

To check your credentials and the gateway URL in one call, ask the gateway to describe your key:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

info = UltraRouter().key.get()
print(info.mode, info.scopes, info.workspace_id)
```

- [Configuration and authentication](configuration.md)
- [Chat completions](chat-completions.md)
- [Plug-and-play learning](learning.md)

<!-- file: docs/configuration.md -->

# Configuration and authentication

## API keys

Every request is authenticated with an ultrarouter API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer
<key>`. Keys look like `ur_sk_live_...` (production traffic) or `ur_sk_test_...` (testing).
Pass the key explicitly or let the client read it from the environment:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()  # ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY, then UR_API_KEY
explicit = UltraRouter(api_key="ur_sk_test_example")
```

If no key is found, construction fails immediately with a `ConfigurationError` whose `code` is
`missing_api_key`. Keep keys out of source control: read them from the environment or a secret
manager. A key's scopes decide which endpoints it may call; `client.key.get()` shows them.

```python
info = client.key.get()
print(info.mode)  # "live" or "test"
print(info.scopes)  # e.g. ["gateway:invoke", "config:read"]
print(info.limits.rps_limit, info.usage.key_spent_micro_usd)
```

## Base URL and self-hosted gateways

The SDK has no default gateway, so you must point it at one: pass `base_url=` or set
`ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL` (then `UR_BASE_URL`). It can be a self-hosted gateway, a staging
environment or a local stack. Constructing a client with no base URL from any source fails
immediately with a `ConfigurationError` whose `code` is `missing_base_url`.

```python
local = UltraRouter(base_url="http://localhost:8080")
internal = UltraRouter(base_url="https://gateway.example.com/v1")  # "/v1" is accepted
print(internal.base_url)  # https://gateway.example.com
```

A trailing slash or `/v1` is removed, because every SDK path already starts with `/v1`.

### Precedence

Explicit constructor arguments win over environment variables. The API key and base URL have no
default: without one from some source, construction fails with a `ConfigurationError`.

| Setting | Argument | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `api_key` | `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY`, `UR_API_KEY` | none (required) |
| Base URL | `base_url` | `ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL`, `UR_BASE_URL` | none (required) |
| Bench tag | `bench` | `UR_BENCH`, `UR_BENCH_RUN`, `UR_BENCH_TRACE` | none |

## Client defaults and per-call overrides

`default_model` and `defaults=` fill in request fields you leave out. A value passed to a call
always wins.

```python
client = UltraRouter(
    default_model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    defaults={
        "call_type": "support-reply",  # group traffic for evals and routing
        "router": "off",  # serve the requested model
        "compression": "off",  # never rewrite prompts
        "provider": {"sort": "latency"},  # provider preferences
        "max_cost_usd": 0.05,  # refuse calls estimated above this, per call
    },
)

reply = client.chat.completions.create(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}])
override = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2",  # per-call model wins
    call_type="escalation",  # per-call call type wins
    ur={"max_cost_usd": 0.20},  # per-call ur.max_cost_usd wins
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}],
)
print(reply.ur.model_served, override.ur.model_served)
```

| Default | Applies to | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default_model` | chat, embeddings | used when `model` is omitted |
| `call_type` | chat, embeddings | a call-type slug |
| `router` | chat | `off`, `candidates` or `auto` (ignored when `autopilot` is set) |
| `compression` | chat | `off`, `semantic_safe`, `adaptive`, or a structured object |
| `provider` | chat | OpenRouter-style provider preferences |
| `max_cost_usd` | chat, embeddings | merged into `ur.max_cost_usd` |

## Autopilot

`autopilot=` states how much routing autonomy you allow, in one argument:

| Intent | Router mode sent | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"audit"` | `off` | observe only; always serve the requested model |
| `"recommend"` | `candidates` | rank an approved candidate list |
| `"auto"` | `auto` | let the router choose, where the gateway allows it |

The intent is also a ceiling: a per-call `router` can lower autonomy but never raise it above the
intent (the SDK clamps the value, and the gateway applies the same rule). `"auto"` expresses
intent; it does not bypass any gateway check.

```python
audit = UltraRouter(autopilot="audit")
print(audit.autopilot.mode)  # "audit"
audit.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    router="auto",  # clamped to "off" by the audit ceiling
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}],
)
readiness = audit.autopilot.status()
print(readiness.state, readiness.observing_call_types)
```

See [Autopilot](autopilot.md).

## Bench tagging

`bench=` tags every request for a Bench suite with `X-UR-Bench-*` headers, so a test run can be
captured and compared later. It accepts a suite slug or a mapping with `suite`, optional `run`
(for example a commit SHA) and optional `trace` (a string, or a callable that returns a fresh id
per request). Without the argument, `UR_BENCH` (+ `UR_BENCH_RUN`, `UR_BENCH_TRACE`) is used.

```python
import uuid

tagged = UltraRouter(
    bench={"suite": "checkout-flow", "run": "abc123", "trace": lambda: uuid.uuid4().hex}
)
tagged.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}]
)

# A per-call tag is sent in the body as ur.bench and wins over the client headers.
tagged.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    bench={"suite": "checkout-flow", "trace": "order-17"},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}],
)
```

Bench capture is meant for test keys. With a live key the client warns once at construction,
because the gateway refuses Bench capture on live keys unless a workspace owner allows it.

## Headers, timeouts and retries

```python
client = UltraRouter(
    default_headers={"X-Team": "search"},  # added to every request
    timeout=30,  # total seconds per call, across retries
    max_retries=4,  # automatic retries for transient failures
)
```

Per call, the OpenAI-compatible methods accept `timeout=`, `max_retries=`, `extra_headers=`,
`extra_query=`, `extra_body=` and `idempotency_key=`; every other method accepts
`options={"timeout": ..., "max_retries": ..., "extra_headers": {...}, ...}`. See
[Retries, timeouts and idempotency](retries-timeouts.md).

## Custom HTTP clients (proxies, mTLS, transports)

Pass your own `httpx.Client` (or `httpx.AsyncClient` for the async client) to control proxies,
certificates, connection limits or transports. The SDK never closes a client you pass in.

```python
import httpx

http = httpx.Client(limits=httpx.Limits(max_connections=20), verify=True)
client = UltraRouter(http_client=http)
client.models.list()
http.close()
```

## Next steps

- [Sync and async clients](clients.md)
- [Errors](errors.md)

<!-- file: docs/clients.md -->

# Sync and async clients

The SDK has two clients with the same surface:

| | `UltraRouter` | `AsyncUltraRouter` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Calls | `client.models.list()` | `await client.models.list()` |
| Streams | `Stream` (`for chunk in stream`) | `AsyncStream` (`async for chunk in stream`) |
| Context manager | `with UltraRouter() as client:` | `async with AsyncUltraRouter() as client:` |
| HTTP client | `httpx.Client` | `httpx.AsyncClient` |
| `as_openai()` | `openai.OpenAI` | `openai.AsyncOpenAI` |

Constructor arguments, namespaces, method names and return types are identical. A few local-only
helpers stay synchronous on the async client because they never touch the network:
`client.reviewer.record(...)` and `client.reviewer.dead_letters()`.

## Lifecycle

A client owns a connection pool. Create one per process (or per worker) and reuse it; close it
when you are done, or use it as a context manager.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

with UltraRouter() as client:
    models = client.models.list()
    print(len(models.data))
# the pool is closed here
```

```python
import asyncio

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncUltraRouter() as client:
        models = await client.models.list()
        print(len(models.data))


asyncio.run(main())
```

Creating a client is cheap, but creating one per request wastes connections. Clients are safe
to share between threads (the sync client) or tasks on one event loop (the async client).

## Concurrency with the async client

```python
import asyncio

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter


async def summarize_all(texts: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    async with AsyncUltraRouter(default_model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini") as client:
        replies = await asyncio.gather(
            *(
                client.chat.completions.create(
                    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": f"Summarize: {text}"}]
                )
                for text in texts
            )
        )
    return [reply.choices[0].message.content or "" for reply in replies]


print(asyncio.run(summarize_all(["first document", "second document"])))
```

To bound concurrency, wrap calls in an `asyncio.Semaphore`; the gateway answers excess traffic
with `rate_limited` (429), which the SDK retries with backoff.

## Per-call settings and `with_options`

Any call can override the timeout, retries and headers. To reuse a set of overrides, derive a
client with `with_options`: it shares the parent's connection pool, and closing it does not close
the pool.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
fast = client.with_options(timeout=5, max_retries=0, default_headers={"X-Priority": "interactive"})
print(fast.timeout, client.timeout)  # 5.0 600.0
fast.models.list()
```

Everything a derived client sends uses its own options, including the outcome events and
reviewer decisions it delivers. What it shares with its parent:

| Shared | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| the connection pool | closing the derived client does not close the pool |
| the outcome store and the reviewer store | an event queued through either client is pending for both; whichever client records or flushes it delivers it with **its own** headers, timeout and retries |
| the preflight cache | a cached preflight answer is reused by both (the grant is never cached) |
| the request-thread limit (synchronous clients) | at most 100 calls in flight across the client and its copies (see [the deadline](retries-timeouts.md#the-time-budget-is-a-real-deadline)) |

Delivering a shared event twice (for example both clients flush at once) is harmless: the event
keeps its identity (`source_event_id`, `event_id`) and outcome deliveries reuse the same
`Idempotency-Key`, so the second delivery is recorded as a duplicate. Construct a separate client
with its own `outcome_store=` and `reviewer_store=` if two configurations must never share pending
events.

```python
fast.outcomes.record("ticket:4812:reply", {"channel": "behavioral", "kind": "accepted"})
print(fast.outcomes.size() == client.outcomes.size())  # True: one shared store
client.outcomes.flush()  # delivered with the parent's options
```

## Bringing your own HTTP client

```python
import httpx

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter, UltraRouter

sync_http = httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(30.0))
client = UltraRouter(http_client=sync_http)
client.models.list()
client.close()  # does not close sync_http: you own it
sync_http.close()

async_client = AsyncUltraRouter(http_client=httpx.AsyncClient())
```

The SDK applies its own total time budget per call (`timeout=`) on top of whatever the HTTP
client is configured with: it is a deadline for the whole call, including reading the body (see
[Retries, timeouts and idempotency](retries-timeouts.md#the-time-budget-is-a-real-deadline)).

<!-- file: docs/chat-completions.md -->

# Chat completions

`client.chat.completions.create(...)` sends `POST /v1/chat/completions`. It accepts the OpenAI
chat parameters plus the ultrarouter extensions, and returns a
[`ChatCompletion`](types-reference.md#chatcompletion).

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You answer in one sentence."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is a call type?"},
    ],
    temperature=0.2,
    max_tokens=200,
)
choice = reply.choices[0]
print(choice.message.content, choice.finish_reason)
print(reply.usage.prompt_tokens, reply.usage.completion_tokens)
```

Model ids are provider-prefixed (`openai/gpt-5.2-mini`); `client.models.list()` lists the ids
your workspace can use.

## Parameters

OpenAI parameters are passed through unchanged: `messages` (required), `model`, `temperature`,
`top_p`, `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens`, `n`, `stop`, `seed`, `presence_penalty`,
`frequency_penalty`, `logprobs`, `top_logprobs`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, `response_format`,
`reasoning_effort`, `stream_options`, `user` and `metadata`.

ultrarouter extensions:

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models` | `list[str]` | ordered fallback models tried if the primary model fails |
| `provider` | mapping | provider preferences: `order`, `sort` (`price`, `throughput`, `latency`), `ignore`, `allow_fallbacks`, `data_collection` |
| `router` | `"off"`, `"candidates"`, `"auto"` | routing mode for this call |
| `compression` | mode or mapping | `off` (default, the prompt is never rewritten), `semantic_safe`, `adaptive`, or `{"mode": ..., "no_compress_fields": [...]}` |
| `call_type` | `str` | the call-type slug this request belongs to |
| `reasoning` | mapping | OpenRouter-style reasoning control (`effort`, `max_tokens`, `exclude`) |
| `ur` | mapping | per-request controls (below) |
| `bench` | `str` or mapping | tag this request for a Bench suite (sent as `ur.bench`) |

The `ur` mapping:

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `max_cost_usd` | refuse the call if its estimated cost exceeds this (raises `MaxCostExceededError`) |
| `trace_id` | group the calls of one multi-step task |
| `artifact` | the artifact key this request contributes to (see [Outcomes](outcomes.md)) |
| `tags` | free-form key/value tags stored with the request |
| `timeout_ms` | gateway-side deadline for this call |
| `prompt_vars` | values for the active hosted prompt's variables (see [Hosted prompts](hosted-prompts.md)) |
| `segments` | label message parts (for example reference material) |
| `manifest` | a context manifest from [`ultrarouter.context`](context-runtime.md) |
| `context_modules` | context modules this call opts into |

```python
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    models=["openai/gpt-5.2"],  # fallback if the primary fails
    provider={"sort": "latency"},
    call_type="support-reply",
    ur={"max_cost_usd": 0.02, "trace_id": "order-1001", "tags": {"team": "support"}},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Where is order 1001?"}],
)
print(reply.ur.routing.fallback_used)
```

Anything the SDK does not model yet can be sent with `extra_body=`; it is merged into the JSON
body last.

```python
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}],
    extra_body={"some_new_option": True},
)
```

## The `ur` response block

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `request_id` | `req_...` id; use it for [feedback](feedback.md), [generation lookup](generation.md) and support |
| `model_served` | the model that actually answered (it can differ from the requested model when routing or fallbacks apply) |
| `provider` | the provider that served it |
| `routing` | `mode`, `fallback_used` and the routing `engine` when one ran |
| `compression` | the compression tier `applied` (`off`, `semantic_safe`, `adaptive`) and its details |
| `cost_usd` | the cost of this call in USD |
| `byok` | whether your own provider key (BYOK) was used |
| `call_type` | the resolved call type, if any |
| `artifact_id` | the artifact the request was bound to, when `ur.artifact` was sent |
| `bench` | the Bench capture status, when the request was tagged |

```python
print(reply.ur.request_id, reply.ur.model_served, reply.ur.provider, reply.ur.cost_usd)
print(reply.ur.routing.mode, reply.ur.compression.applied)
```

## Defaults

Use `default_model` and `defaults=` on the client to avoid repeating values; per-call values win.
See [Configuration](configuration.md#client-defaults-and-per-call-overrides).

```python
client = UltraRouter(default_model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", defaults={"call_type": "support-reply"})
reply = client.chat.completions.create(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}])
```

## Async

```python
import asyncio

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter


async def main() -> str | None:
    async with AsyncUltraRouter() as client:
        reply = await client.chat.completions.create(
            model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}]
        )
        return reply.choices[0].message.content


print(asyncio.run(main()))
```

- [Errors](errors.md): which exceptions `create` can raise

<!-- file: docs/streaming.md -->

# Streaming

Pass `stream=True` to `client.chat.completions.create` to receive the answer as server-sent
events. The sync client returns a [`Stream`](api-reference.md#stream), the async client an
[`AsyncStream`](api-reference.md#asyncstream). Each item is a
[`ChatCompletionChunk`](types-reference.md#chatcompletionchunk).

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a haiku about routers."}],
    stream=True,
)
with stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        for choice in chunk.choices:
            if choice.delta.content:
                print(choice.delta.content, end="", flush=True)
print()
```

## The final chunk: usage and `ur`

The last chunk before the end of the stream has empty `choices` and carries `usage` and the `ur`
block. The stream object also keeps them, so you can read them after iterating:

```python
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi."}],
    stream=True,
)
text = stream.text()  # consume the stream and join the content deltas
print(text)
print(stream.usage.total_tokens if stream.usage else None)
print(stream.ur.request_id if stream.ur else None)
```

`stream.request_id` is available as soon as the stream opens, before the first chunk: it is read
from the `x-ur-request-id` response header (and falls back to the final `ur` block, then to the id
you sent with `request_id=`). See [Plug-and-play learning](learning.md#correlation).

## Closing early

Leaving a `with` block (or calling `close()`) closes the HTTP response even if you stop reading
early. Iterating to the end closes it too.

```python
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me a long story."}],
    stream=True,
)
first = next(stream)
stream.close()
print(first.choices[0].delta.role)
```

## Async streaming

```python
import asyncio

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncUltraRouter() as client:
        stream = await client.chat.completions.create(
            model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Count to five."}],
            stream=True,
        )
        async with stream:
            async for chunk in stream:
                if chunk.choices and chunk.choices[0].delta.content:
                    print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content, end="")
        print()
        print(stream.ur.cost_usd if stream.ur else None)


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Errors during a stream

- An error before the first byte (for example `401`, `403 model_unpriced`, `429`) raises from
  `create(...)` itself, as a typed error.
- An error after the stream started arrives as an `event: error` frame and is raised from the
  iterator as the same typed error. Content received before it remains valid.
- Streams are **not** retried automatically and carry no idempotency key; retry yourself if a
  restart is acceptable for your use case.
- `timeout` is the deadline for the stream to *start* (connection and response headers), then the
  longest silence allowed between chunks; a longer silence raises `APITimeoutError` from the
  iterator. The total length of a stream is not limited. See
  [Timeouts in streams](retries-timeouts.md#timeouts-in-streams).
- A connection that breaks mid-stream raises `APIConnectionError` from the iterator.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouterError

try:
    for chunk in client.chat.completions.create(
        model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}], stream=True
    ):
        pass
except UltraRouterError as exc:
    print("stream failed:", exc.code, exc.request_id)
```

## Tool calls in a stream

Tool calls arrive as fragments in `choice.delta.tool_calls`; join the `function.arguments`
fragments per `index`. See [Tools](tools.md#streaming-tool-calls).

---

<!-- file: docs/tools.md -->

# Tools (function calling)

Tools use the OpenAI format: describe functions in `tools`, let the model choose with
`tool_choice`, run the function yourself, and send the result back as a `tool` message.

```python
import json

from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()

tools = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "get_order_status",
            "description": "Look up the shipping status of an order.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["order_id"],
            },
        },
    }
]

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Where is order 1001?"}]
first = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=messages, tools=tools, tool_choice="auto"
)
message = first.choices[0].message
print(first.choices[0].finish_reason)  # "tool_calls"
```

`message.tool_calls` is a list of plain dicts in the OpenAI shape
(`{"id", "type": "function", "function": {"name", "arguments"}}`); `arguments` is a JSON string.

```python
def get_order_status(order_id: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"order_id": order_id, "status": "shipped"}


messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": message.content, "tool_calls": message.tool_calls})
for call in message.tool_calls or []:
    arguments = json.loads(call["function"]["arguments"])
    result = get_order_status(**arguments)
    messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": json.dumps(result)})

final = client.chat.completions.create(model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=messages, tools=tools)
print(final.choices[0].message.content)
```

`tool_choice` accepts `"auto"`, `"none"`, `"required"` or `{"type": "function", "function":
{"name": "get_order_status"}}`.

If the selected model cannot use tools, the gateway refuses before calling it and the SDK raises
`CapabilityUnsupportedError` (code `capability_unsupported`) naming the missing capability; it
does not silently switch models.

## Streaming tool calls

When streaming, tool calls arrive in fragments on `choice.delta.tool_calls`
([`ChunkDeltaToolCall`](types-reference.md#chunkdeltatoolcall)); the first fragment of each call
carries its `id` and `function.name`, later fragments append to `function.arguments`.

```python
calls: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Where is order 1001?"}],
    tools=tools,
    stream=True,
)
for chunk in stream:
    for choice in chunk.choices:
        for fragment in choice.delta.tool_calls or []:
            entry = calls.setdefault(fragment.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""})
            entry["id"] = fragment.id or entry["id"]
            if fragment.function is not None:
                entry["name"] = fragment.function.name or entry["name"]
                entry["arguments"] += fragment.function.arguments or ""

for call in calls.values():
    print(call["name"], json.loads(call["arguments"]))
```

---

<!-- file: docs/structured-outputs.md -->

# Structured outputs

Ask for JSON with `response_format`. Two forms are supported:

- `{"type": "json_object"}`: any valid JSON object;
- `{"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": ..., "schema": {...}}}`: JSON that follows
  your schema.

```python
import json

from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()

response_format = {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {
        "name": "ticket_triage",
        "schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "category": {"type": "string", "enum": ["billing", "shipping", "other"]},
                "urgent": {"type": "boolean"},
            },
            "required": ["category", "urgent"],
        },
    },
}

reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "My package never arrived and I need it today."}],
    response_format=response_format,
)
data = json.loads(reply.choices[0].message.content or "{}")
print(data["category"], data["urgent"])
```

## Parsing into pydantic

Validate the content with your own pydantic model to get typed data and a clear error when the
output does not match:

```python
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel


class Triage(BaseModel):
    category: Literal["billing", "shipping", "other"]
    urgent: bool


triage = Triage.model_validate_json(reply.choices[0].message.content or "{}")
print(triage.category)
```

You can generate the schema from the model instead of writing it by hand:

```python
schema_format = {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {"name": "triage", "schema": Triage.model_json_schema()},
}
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Refund my double charge."}],
    response_format=schema_format,
)
print(Triage.model_validate_json(reply.choices[0].message.content or "{}"))
```

## When the model cannot do it

If the selected model does not support the requested format, the gateway refuses before calling
it and the SDK raises `CapabilityUnsupportedError`. It never downgrades the format silently. Pick
a model whose `capabilities` (from `client.models.retrieve(model_id)`) include structured output.

---

<!-- file: docs/embeddings.md -->

# Embeddings

`client.embeddings.create(...)` sends `POST /v1/embeddings` and returns a
[`CreateEmbeddingResponse`](types-reference.md#createembeddingresponse).

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
response = client.embeddings.create(
    model="openai/text-embedding-3-small",
    input=["The quick brown fox", "jumps over the lazy dog"],
)
for item in response.data:
    print(item.index, len(item.embedding))
print(response.usage.total_tokens, response.ur.cost_usd)
```

`input` is a string or a list of strings. Results come back in input order (`item.index`).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | text or list of texts (required) |
| `model` | embedding model id; falls back to `default_model` |
| `dimensions` | shorten vectors, for models that support it |
| `encoding_format` | `"float"` (default, lists of floats) or `"base64"` (packed little-endian float32) |
| `user`, `metadata` | passed through |
| `call_type`, `ur`, `bench` | as for chat completions |

## Base64 vectors

Base64 output is smaller on the wire. Decode it with the standard library:

```python
import base64
import struct

packed = client.embeddings.create(
    model="openai/text-embedding-3-small", input="hello", encoding_format="base64", dimensions=8
)
raw = base64.b64decode(packed.data[0].embedding)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
vector = struct.unpack(f"<{len(raw) // 4}f", raw)
print(len(vector))
```

## Async

```python
import asyncio

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter


async def embed(texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
    async with AsyncUltraRouter() as client:
        response = await client.embeddings.create(
            model="openai/text-embedding-3-small", input=texts
        )
    return [list(item.embedding) for item in response.data]  # type: ignore[arg-type]


print(len(asyncio.run(embed(["a", "b", "c"]))))
```

The `ur` block on an embeddings response has the request id, served model, provider, routing,
cost and BYOK flag (no compression block: inputs are never rewritten).

---

<!-- file: docs/models.md -->

# Models and key info

## List the catalog

`client.models.list()` (`GET /v1/models`) returns a [`ModelList`](types-reference.md#modellist)
of the models your workspace can use, with pricing and capabilities. Filter by provider or
capability:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
catalog = client.models.list(provider="openai")
for model in catalog.data:
    print(
        model.id,
        model.context_length,
        model.pricing.input_usd_per_1m,
        model.pricing.output_usd_per_1m,
    )

tool_models = client.models.list(capability="tools")
print([m.id for m in tool_models.data])
```

Prices are reported per million tokens, both as integer micro-USD (`input_micro_usd_per_1m`)
and as USD floats (`input_usd_per_1m`).

## One model and its offers

`client.models.retrieve(model_id)` (`GET /v1/models/{id}`) returns a
[`ModelDetail`](types-reference.md#modeldetail) with every provider offer for the model. The
provider-prefixed id (with its `/`) is passed as-is; the SDK encodes it.

```python
detail = client.models.retrieve("openai/gpt-5.2")
print(detail.name, detail.capabilities, detail.weights)
for offer in detail.offers:
    print(offer.provider, offer.pricing.input_usd_per_1m, offer.hosting_jurisdiction)
```

An unknown id raises `NotFoundError`.

## Inspect your API key

`client.key.get()` (`GET /v1/key`) describes the key the client uses: its mode (`live` or
`test`), scopes, limits and spend this period. It is also the simplest way to check
configuration, since a wrong key raises `AuthenticationError`.

```python
info = client.key.get()
print(info.name, info.prefix, info.mode, info.scopes)
print(info.limits.spend_cap_micro_usd, info.usage.key_spent_micro_usd, info.usage.period)
```

---

<!-- file: docs/openai-compatibility.md -->

# OpenAI compatibility

The gateway speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions, Embeddings and Models APIs under `/v1`. You can
use this SDK's OpenAI-shaped methods, or keep the official `openai` package and point it at the
gateway.

## Option 1: this SDK's OpenAI-shaped surface

`client.chat.completions.create`, `client.embeddings.create`, `client.models.list` and
`client.models.retrieve` take the same arguments as the `openai` package (plus the ultrarouter
extensions) and accept the same per-call options (`timeout`, `max_retries`, `extra_headers`,
`extra_query`, `extra_body`). Responses are typed pydantic models with the `ur` block as a
typed attribute.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content, reply.ur.cost_usd)
```

## Option 2: the `openai` package, configured by `as_openai()`

Install the `openai` extra (see [Installation](installation.md#the-openai-extra)), then:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

openai_client = UltraRouter().as_openai()
reply = openai_client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)
print(reply.model_extra["ur"]["request_id"])  # the ur block arrives as an extra field
```

`as_openai()` returns `openai.OpenAI(base_url=f"{base_url}/v1", api_key=..., default_headers=...)`
with the client's default headers (including any Bench tag headers). The async client returns an
`openai.AsyncOpenAI`. Pass any callable that accepts those keyword arguments to build something
else instead, such as a test double: `client.as_openai(FakeOpenAI)`.

## Option 3: configure `openai` yourself

Nothing is special about `as_openai()`; this is equivalent:

```python
import os

import openai

manual = openai.OpenAI(
    base_url=os.environ["ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY"],
)
print(manual.models.list().data[0].id)
```

To correlate calls made through the `openai` package (for outcome reporting), mint the request id
up front and send it as a header; `ultrarouter.request_id_of(reply)` reads it back from the `ur`
block the gateway adds:

```python
from ultrarouter import correlation_headers, new_request_id, request_id_of

request_id = new_request_id()
reply = manual.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}],
    extra_headers=correlation_headers(request_id=request_id),
)
assert request_id_of(reply) == request_id
```

See [Plug-and-play learning](learning.md).

## Migrating from `openai`

| `openai` | `ultrarouter` |
| --- | --- |
| `OpenAI(api_key=...)` | `UltraRouter(api_key=...)` (`ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY`) |
| `OpenAI(base_url=...)` | `UltraRouter(base_url=...)` (`ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL`; `/v1` optional) |
| `AsyncOpenAI` | `AsyncUltraRouter` |
| `client.chat.completions.create(...)` | same |
| `client.embeddings.create(...)` | same |
| `client.models.list()` / `retrieve(id)` | same |
| `openai.APIError` and subclasses | `ultrarouter.UltraRouterError` and subclasses (`RateLimitError`, `AuthenticationError`, `NotFoundError`, ...) |
| `model="gpt-4o"` | provider-prefixed ids, for example `model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini"` |

Differences to keep in mind:

- Model ids are provider-prefixed. `client.models.list()` shows what is available.
- Errors carry the gateway's stable `code` (for example `model_unpriced`) and `request_id`.
- Responses include `ur` (served model, provider, routing, cost); with the `openai` package it is
  in `model_extra["ur"]`.
- The OpenAI Assistants, Files, Images and Audio APIs are not part of the gateway.

---

<!-- file: docs/passthrough.md -->

# Native passthrough: the official OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs through your gateway

The gateway exposes two routes that forward a provider request **verbatim** and return the
provider response **unchanged**:

- `POST /v1/responses` — the OpenAI **Responses API**;
- `POST /v1/messages` — the Anthropic **Messages API**.

The JSON body is passed through untouched (no routing, no compression, no model remapping, no
field injection); the gateway meters the call, applies your spend caps and captures it, then hands
back the provider's own object. The model id in the body is the model that is called, so it is the
provider's native id (`gpt-6-sol`, `claude-opus-5-5`), not a provider-prefixed ultrarouter id.

The intended client for these routes is the **official** `openai` and `anthropic` SDK: point it at
the gateway by changing only the base URL and the key. You can also reach them from this SDK's raw
request surface (below).

## Point the official SDK at the gateway

Each official SDK reads a base-URL environment variable. Set it to your gateway (no trailing path
for Anthropic; the OpenAI SDK expects the `/v1` suffix), and put your ultrarouter key where that
SDK puts the provider key:

```bash
# OpenAI SDK -> gateway (ultrarouter key travels as Authorization: Bearer)
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080/v1"      # or https://gateway.example.com/v1
export OPENAI_API_KEY="ur_sk_live_your_key"

# Anthropic SDK -> gateway (ultrarouter key travels as x-api-key)
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080"      # or https://gateway.example.com
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="ur_sk_live_your_key"
```

Key placement: the OpenAI SDK sends the key as `Authorization: Bearer`; the Anthropic SDK sends it
as `x-api-key`. The gateway accepts the ultrarouter key either way (`Authorization: Bearer` **or**
`x-api-key`). Your own provider key is never forwarded upstream — the platform or BYOK key is
injected server-side.

With the environment set, the official SDKs call the gateway with no code change:

<!-- doctest: skip — the official openai and anthropic packages are not dependencies of this SDK; this block shows the call shape -->
```python
from anthropic import Anthropic
from openai import OpenAI

# OpenAI Responses API, forwarded verbatim through the gateway:
openai_client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
response = openai_client.responses.create(model="gpt-6-sol", input="Summarise this ticket.")

# Anthropic Messages API, forwarded verbatim through the gateway:
anthropic_client = Anthropic()  # reads ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
message = anthropic_client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=256,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this ticket."}],
)
```

## The ur extension headers

The ultrarouter extensions ride **request headers** so the body stays a pristine provider payload.
Pass them through the official SDK's per-request `extra_headers` (or `default_headers`):

| Request header | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `X-UR-Call-Type` | The call-type stage this call belongs to. |
| `X-UR-Trace` | JSON `{"run", "case", "stage", "attempt"}` tying the call to a run. |
| `X-UR-Timeout-Ms` | Upstream timeout in milliseconds, clamped to 1 s–600 s (default 300 s). |

Every non-streaming passthrough response carries two **response headers**:

| Response header | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `X-UR-Request-Id` | The ultrarouter request id; keep it for feedback, stats and support. |
| `X-UR-Cost-Micro-USD` | The booked cost of the call, in integer micro-USD. |

When the request sets `stream: true`, the upstream SSE bytes are forwarded frame by frame.

## Reach the passthrough routes from this SDK

The typed methods of `UltraRouter` do not wrap these routes (the whole point is to forward an opaque
body), but the client's raw request surface does. Build an
[`APIRequest`](api-reference.md#apirequest) and call `request` for the raw response (so you can read
the `X-UR-*` headers), `request_json` for the decoded body, or `request_model` to validate it into
a type. The SDK still adds authentication, the deadline, retries and the idempotency key for you.

```python
from ultrarouter import APIRequest, UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()  # reads ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY and ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL

response = client.request(
    APIRequest(
        "POST",
        "/v1/responses",
        body={"model": "gpt-6-sol", "input": "Summarise this ticket."},
        headers={
            "X-UR-Call-Type": "support-reply",
            "X-UR-Trace": '{"run": "r-7", "case": "c-3", "stage": "draft", "attempt": 1}',
            "X-UR-Timeout-Ms": "30000",
        },
    )
)
request_id = response.headers["X-UR-Request-Id"]
cost_micro_usd = int(response.headers["X-UR-Cost-Micro-USD"])
responses_object = response.json()  # the OpenAI Responses object, unchanged
print(request_id, cost_micro_usd, responses_object["output"][0]["content"][0]["text"])
client.close()
```

The Anthropic Messages route works the same way; `request_json` returns the decoded body:

```python
from ultrarouter import APIRequest, UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
message = client.request_json(
    APIRequest(
        "POST",
        "/v1/messages",
        body={
            "model": "claude-opus-5-5",
            "max_tokens": 256,
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this ticket."}],
        },
        headers={"X-UR-Call-Type": "support-reply"},
    )
)
print(message["role"], message["stop_reason"], message["content"][0]["text"])
client.close()
```

`AsyncUltraRouter` has the same `request`, `request_json` and `request_model` methods; `await` them.
A non-`None` `body` is sent as JSON automatically, so you rarely set `has_body` yourself.

---

<!-- file: docs/call-types.md -->

# Call types

A *call type* groups requests that do the same job (for example `support-reply` or
`ticket-classifier`). Routing configuration, evals, recommendations, hosted prompts and
learned context are all attached to a call type. Send `call_type="<slug>"` on requests (or set it
in the client `defaults`) to attribute traffic.

Reading call types needs a key with `config:read`; changing them needs `config:write`.

## Create, list, get

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()

created = client.call_types.create(
    slug="support-reply",
    config={"model_pin": "openai/gpt-5.2-mini", "fallbacks": ["openai/gpt-5.2"]},
)
print(created.id, created.slug, created.lifecycle_state)

for call_type in client.call_types.list().data:
    print(call_type.slug, call_type.current_config_version)

same = client.call_types.get("support-reply")  # by slug or by id
print(same.config.model_pin if same.config else None)
```

## Update the configuration

`update` writes a new configuration version. Only the arguments you pass are sent; for
`model_pin`, `router_mode`, `compression_mode` and `provider_prefs`, passing `None` clears the
setting.

```python
updated = client.call_types.update(
    "support-reply",
    router_mode="candidates",
    compression_mode="off",
    fallbacks=["openai/gpt-5.2"],
)
cleared = client.call_types.update("support-reply", model_pin=None)  # unpin the model
print(updated.config.version if updated.config else None)
```

| Setting | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `model_pin` | a model id, or `None` to unpin |
| `router_mode` | `off`, `pinned`, `candidates`, `auto`, or `None` |
| `compression_mode` | `off`, `semantic_safe`, `adaptive` (legacy aliases `lossless` and `auto` are accepted), or `None` |
| `fallbacks` | ordered fallback model ids |
| `provider_prefs` | provider preferences mapping, or `None` |
| `learned_context_delivery` | `gateway_inject_after_stable_prefix` or `off` |
| `case_precedents_enabled` | `True` / `False` |
| `self_improve_mode` | `off`, `assist`, `autopilot` |
| `self_improve_guardrails` | `{"surfaces": [...], "max_cost_per_success_micro_usd": ...}` |

## Evals

Trigger an eval run now, or list past runs:

```python
run = client.call_types.enqueue_eval("support-reply", mode="request")
if run.enqueued:
    print("enqueued", run.run_id, run.candidate_count)
else:
    print("not enqueued:", run.reason, run.prior_run_id)

for eval_run in client.call_types.list_evals("support-reply").data:
    print(eval_run.id, eval_run.status, eval_run.item_count)
```

An eval trigger that is not enqueued returns a documented reason (`no_golden_set`,
`no_candidates`, `deduped`, ...). A de-duplicated trigger names the run it joined in
`prior_run_id`, so you can follow it.

## Recommendations

```python
recommendations = client.call_types.list_recommendations("support-reply")
print(recommendations.keys())
```

The recommendation payload is not described by the API specification yet, so it is returned as
a plain `dict`.

## Related

- [Hosted prompts](hosted-prompts.md) (`client.call_types.prompts`)
- [Verified memory](verified-memory.md) (`client.call_types.verified_memory`)
- [Preflight](preflight.md): what the gateway would decide for a call type
