<!-- file: docs/hosted-prompts.md -->

# Hosted prompts

A hosted prompt is a versioned template stored on a call type. Versions are immutable; one
version at most is *active*. The gateway can apply the active prompt to proxied requests, and
any caller can fetch it to render it locally.

Templates use `{{name}}` slots. Each declared variable is `required` or optional; a missing
required variable is a named refusal (`prompt_variables_missing`), never a silent blank.

## Create, activate, roll back

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()

version = client.call_types.prompts.create(
    "support-reply",
    template="You are a {{tone}} support agent for {{brand}}.",
    variables=[{"name": "tone", "required": False}, {"name": "brand", "required": True}],
)
print(version.version, version.active, version.content_sha256)

activation = client.call_types.prompts.activate(
    "support-reply", version.version, gateway_apply=True
)
print(activation.active_version, activation.gateway_apply)
```

`gateway_apply=True` makes the gateway apply the prompt to proxied requests for this call type;
`False` serves it only through `get_prompt` and preflight. Activating an older version is the
rollback. `deactivate` returns the call type to code-owned prompts.

```python
history = client.call_types.prompts.list("support-reply")
print(history.active_version, [v.version for v in history.data])

older = client.call_types.prompts.get("support-reply", 1)
print(older.template)

client.call_types.prompts.deactivate("support-reply")
```

## Supplying variables on proxied requests

When the gateway applies a hosted prompt, pass the variable values in `ur.prompt_vars`:

```python
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    call_type="support-reply",
    ur={"prompt_vars": {"brand": "Northwind", "tone": "friendly"}},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Where is my order?"}],
)
```

A missing required variable raises `PromptVariablesMissingError` (HTTP 400) before any model is
called.

## Fetching and rendering locally

If you call your model provider yourself, fetch the active version and render it with the same
rule the gateway uses:

```python
from ultrarouter import render_prompt

prompt = client.get_prompt("support-reply")  # None when the call type is code-owned
if prompt is not None:
    system = render_prompt(prompt, {"brand": "Northwind", "tone": "friendly"})
    print(prompt.version, system)
```

`get_prompt` reuses the cached preflight read, so calling it often is cheap. See
[Prompt rendering](prompt-render.md) for the exact rules.

## Onboarding proposal

The gateway can propose a template inferred from the system prompts you already send:

```python
proposal = client.call_types.prompts.proposal("support-reply")
if proposal.available:
    print(proposal.template, [v.name for v in proposal.variables])
else:
    print("no proposal:", proposal.reason)
```

---

<!-- file: docs/prompt-render.md -->

# Prompt rendering

`render_prompt` and `render_hosted_prompt_result` fill a hosted prompt template exactly the way
the gateway does, so text rendered on your side matches what a proxied call would send. They are
pure functions (no network), available from `ultrarouter` and `ultrarouter.context`.

## Rules

1. Every `{{name}}` slot is replaced by `str(value)`. Whitespace inside the braces is allowed
   (`{{ name }}`); names are letters, digits and underscores only, so `{{user.name}}` is not a slot.
2. A declared **required** variable that is missing or `None` is a refusal listing every missing
   name (sorted). It is never rendered as an empty string.
3. A missing optional variable, and a slot that is not declared at all, render as `""`.

## `render_prompt`: text or an exception

```python
from ultrarouter import PromptVariablesMissingError, render_prompt

prompt = {
    "template": "You are a {{tone}} assistant for {{brand}}.",
    "variables": [{"name": "tone", "required": False}, {"name": "brand", "required": True}],
}

print(render_prompt(prompt, {"brand": "Northwind", "tone": "concise"}))
print(render_prompt(prompt, {"brand": "Northwind"}))  # optional tone renders as ""

try:
    render_prompt(prompt, {"tone": "concise"})
except PromptVariablesMissingError as exc:
    print(exc.code, exc.missing)  # prompt_variables_missing ['brand']
```

`prompt` can be the `PreflightPrompt` returned by `client.get_prompt(...)`, a hosted prompt
version from `client.call_types.prompts.get(...)`, or any mapping or object with `template` and
`variables`.

## `render_hosted_prompt_result`: a result value

```python
from ultrarouter import render_hosted_prompt_result

ok = render_hosted_prompt_result(
    "Hello {{name}}", [{"name": "name", "required": True}], {"name": "Ana"}
)
missing = render_hosted_prompt_result("Hello {{name}}", [{"name": "name", "required": True}], {})
print(ok)  # {'ok': True, 'text': 'Hello Ana'}
print(missing)  # {'ok': False, 'missing': ['name']}
```

The client-side `PromptVariablesMissingError` has `status == 0` (nothing was sent); the same
class is raised with `status == 400` when the gateway refuses a proxied request for the same
reason.

---

<!-- file: docs/verified-memory.md -->

# Verified memory

Verified memory lets the gateway answer a request for a call type from the workspace's verified
past cases, when a calibrated rule says it is safe to do so. It is enabled per call type, can be
inspected at any time, and has a kill switch.

## Enable

Enabling calibrates the rule against the verified cases. If the call type does not qualify, the
response says why (`reason`, for example `pool_empty` or `calibration_below_target`) and nothing
is enabled.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()

result = client.call_types.verified_memory.enable("ticket-classifier", target_precision=0.95)
if result.enabled:
    print("enabled; calibration:", result.calibration)
else:
    print("not enabled:", result.reason, result.message)
```

## Inspect

```python
status = client.call_types.verified_memory.get("ticket-classifier")
print(status.enabled, status.config_version)
if status.servable is not None:
    print("servable:", status.servable.ok, status.servable.reason)
if status.setting is not None:
    print("target precision:", status.setting.target_precision)
```

`servable` is a live check: a stored setting that cannot be served right now (for example after
consent was revoked) is reported with a named reason rather than shown as off.

## Disable (kill switch)

```python
disabled = client.call_types.verified_memory.disable("ticket-classifier")
print(disabled.changed, disabled.previous_lever_version)
```

Responses served from verified memory carry `ur.verified_memory` (the rule version, pool hash,
agreement and the case ids used) on the chat completion.

---

<!-- file: docs/feedback.md -->

# Feedback

Attach a thumbs-up (`1`) or thumbs-down (`-1`) to a served request, with optional tags and a
comment. Use the request id from `response.ur.request_id`.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize my invoice."}]
)

feedback = client.requests.feedback(
    reply.ur.request_id,
    rating=-1,
    tags=["wrong-total"],
    comment="The total did not include tax.",
)
print(feedback.id, feedback.rating, feedback.tags, feedback.created_at)
```

`POST /v1/requests/{id}/feedback` answers with `{"feedback": {...}}`; the SDK unwraps it and
returns the [`Feedback`](types-reference.md#feedback) record.

Feedback is a lightweight signal attached to one request. To record what happened to the thing
your application produced (accepted, edited, resolved later), use
[Outcomes and artifacts](outcomes.md), which also supports delayed and batched events.

The request row is written asynchronously after the response; feedback sent immediately after
the call can briefly raise `NotFoundError`. Retry after a short delay in that case.

```python
import asyncio

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter


async def rate(request_id: str) -> None:
    async with AsyncUltraRouter() as client:
        await client.requests.feedback(request_id, rating=1)


asyncio.run(rate(reply.ur.request_id))
```

---

<!-- file: docs/generation.md -->

# Generation lookup

`client.generation.get(request_id)` (`GET /v1/generation?id=...`) returns the post-hoc record
of one request: tokens, cost, timing, the routing decision (including fallback attempts),
compression details, exposure and any outcomes recorded against it.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    models=["openai/gpt-5.2"],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)

stats = client.generation.get(reply.ur.request_id)
print(stats.status, stats.model_requested, stats.model_served, stats.provider)
print(stats.tokens.input, stats.tokens.output, stats.tokens.cached, stats.tokens.total)
print(stats.cost.total_usd, stats.cost.total_micro_usd)
print(stats.timing.ttfb_ms, stats.timing.latency_ms)
print(stats.routing_decision)  # e.g. {"attempts": [...]} when fallbacks were tried
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `ok`, `error` or `cancelled` |
| `error_class` | the error class when the request failed |
| `tokens` | `input`, `output`, `cached`, `total` |
| `cost` | `total_usd` and `total_micro_usd` (integer micro-USD) |
| `timing` | `ttfb_ms` and `latency_ms` |
| `routing_decision` | the routing record, including fallback attempts |
| `compression` | what compression did, if anything |
| `exposure`, `lever` | experiment arm and learned-context details, when applicable |
| `outcomes` | outcome events recorded against the request |

The record is written asynchronously, so a lookup right after the call can raise
`NotFoundError`; retry briefly:

```python
import time

from ultrarouter import NotFoundError


def generation_with_retry(request_id: str, attempts: int = 5):
    for attempt in range(attempts):
        try:
            return client.generation.get(request_id)
        except NotFoundError:
            time.sleep(0.2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise TimeoutError(f"no generation record for {request_id}")


print(generation_with_retry(reply.ur.request_id).status)
```

---

<!-- file: docs/autopilot.md -->

# Autopilot

Autopilot is a one-argument way to state how much routing autonomy your application allows:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter(autopilot="audit")
print(client.autopilot.mode)  # "audit"
```

| Intent | Router mode | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"audit"` | `off` | observe traffic; always serve the requested model |
| `"recommend"` | `candidates` | rank an approved list of candidate models |
| `"auto"` | `auto` | let the router choose where the gateway allows it |

The intent is a ceiling for the call's `router` parameter: a call may lower autonomy (for
example `router="off"` under `"auto"`) but a request for more is clamped down to the intent.
The gateway enforces the same rule and its own readiness requirements, so `"auto"` expresses what
you allow, not a bypass.

```python
auto = UltraRouter(autopilot="auto")
reply = auto.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    router="off",  # this call opts out of routing
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}],
)
print(reply.ur.routing.mode)
```

## Readiness report

`client.autopilot.status()` (`GET /v1/audit/readiness`) is a read-only report of what the gateway
has observed: per call type, the request count, spend, models and providers seen, lifecycle
state, confidence and the evidence still missing. It changes nothing.

```python
report = client.autopilot.status()
print(report.state, report.total_requests, report.total_spend_micro_usd)
for row in report.call_types:
    print(row.slug, row.lifecycle_state, row.confidence, row.requests, row.evidence_gaps)
```

`report.opportunities` lists candidate model changes as discovery hints; they are estimates
from list prices, not results. Use [Bench](bench.md) or evals to compare candidates on your own
traffic before changing anything.

---

<!-- file: docs/bench.md -->

# Bench

Bench compares candidate models against your current configuration on your own captured
traffic: capture requests into a *suite*, freeze them into datasets, run a paired comparison
within a budget, and read an immutable report. In CI, pin a baseline and gate changes on a
compare run.

Bench needs a key with the `bench:run` scope (freezing needs `config:write`). Use a test key:
the gateway refuses Bench capture on live keys unless a workspace owner allows it.

## 1. Capture traffic into a suite

Tag requests with a suite, either for the whole client or per call:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter(bench={"suite": "checkout-assistant", "run": "commit-abc123"})
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    call_type="support-reply",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Can I change my delivery address?"}],
)
print(reply.ur.bench)  # capture status for this request

status = client.bench.status("checkout-assistant")
print(status.total_captured, [ct.captured for ct in status.call_types])
```

## 2. Freeze, add expectations and outcomes

```python
frozen = client.bench.freeze("checkout-assistant", max_items=500)
for dataset in frozen.datasets:
    print(dataset.call_type_id, dataset.card.unique_count, dataset.card.power_plan.summary)
for warning in frozen.warnings or []:
    print("warning:", warning.code, warning.message)

client.bench.expect(
    "checkout-assistant",
    [
        {
            "kind": "json_schema",
            "call_type": "support-reply",
            "config": {"required_fields": ["answer"]},
        }
    ],
)
client.bench.record([{"trace": "order-1001", "passed": True}], suite="checkout-assistant")
```

## 3. Run

Start with a dry run: it estimates cost and says, per call type, whether the run can proceed
(`runnable`, `not_runnable`, `deduped`, `budget_queued`) without spending anything.

```python
estimate = client.bench.run(
    suite="checkout-assistant",
    max_cost_usd=5,
    candidates=["openai/gpt-5.2"],
    dry_run=True,
)
print(estimate.estimate_usd, [(d.call_type_id, d.disposition) for d in estimate.dispositions])

run = client.bench.run(
    suite="checkout-assistant",
    max_cost_usd=5,
    candidates=["openai/gpt-5.2"],
    wait=True,  # poll until complete or failed
    poll_interval=2.0,
    wait_timeout=600,
)
print(run.status)
```

With `wait=True` the return type is `BenchRunTrigger | BenchRun` (a dry run, or a trigger that
created no run, comes back unchanged). Narrow it before using run-only fields:

```python
from ultrarouter.types import BenchRun

assert isinstance(run, BenchRun)
print(run.id, [eval_run.status for eval_run in run.runs])
```

`max_cost_usd` is a hard budget for the run. `wait=True` returns the finished
[`BenchRun`](types-reference.md#benchrun) (or raises `APITimeoutError` after `wait_timeout`);
without it you get the [`BenchRunTrigger`](types-reference.md#benchruntrigger) and can poll with
`client.bench.get(run_id)` or `client.bench.wait(run_id)`.

## 4. Read the report

```python
report = client.bench.report(run.id)
print(report.status, report.content_hash)
for call_type in report.call_types:
    for verdict in call_type.verdicts:
        print(call_type.call_type_id, verdict.model, verdict.overall, verdict.reasons)
print(report.limitations)

markdown = client.bench.report(run.id, format="md")  # a Markdown export (str)
bundle = client.bench.report(run.id, format="bundle")  # an offline-verifiable evidence bundle (str)
```

Reports state their evidence level and limitations; read those before acting on a result.

## 5. Baseline and compare gate (CI)

Pin a completed run as the suite baseline, then run a compare run for a change and read the
tri-state gate (`pass`, `fail`, `inconclusive`):

```python
client.bench.baseline(run.id)
compare = client.bench.run(
    suite="checkout-assistant",
    max_cost_usd=5,
    compare=True,
    baseline_run_id=run.id,
    wait=True,
)
assert isinstance(compare, BenchRun)
gate = client.bench.gate(compare.id)
print(gate.verdict, gate.reasons)
if gate.verdict != "pass":
    raise SystemExit(2)
```

## Async

Every method has an async twin on `AsyncUltraRouter`, including `run(wait=True)` and `wait()`.

---

<!-- file: docs/outcomes.md -->

# Outcomes and artifacts

The outcome ledger records what happened **after** a model answered. Your application produces
*artifacts* (a draft reply, an answer, a forecast, an extraction); *outcome events* say what
became of them: accepted, edited, resolved correctly, clicked, and so on, instantly or days
later. Events carry ids, hashes and values, never prompt or completion text, and the server
assigns their provenance from your API key.

These endpoints need a key with the `outcomes:write` scope.

## Artifact types and objectives

Declare what "it worked" means for a kind of artifact once:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
artifact_type = client.artifact_types.upsert(
    name="support-reply",
    archetype="draft",
    objective={
        "metric": "acceptance_rate",
        "unit": "ratio",
        "direction": "higher_is_better",
        "resolution_criteria": "the agent sends the reply without edits",
        "source": "helpdesk",
        "window": "P7D",
    },
)
print(artifact_type.id, artifact_type.version)
```

`archetype` is one of `forecast`, `recommendation`, `draft`, `extraction`, `answer`, `action`.
Upserting again with a different objective appends a new version.

## Artifacts

`create` upserts by your stable `key`, so calling it twice with the same key returns the same
artifact.

```python
artifact = client.artifacts.create(
    key="ticket:4812:reply",
    archetype="draft",
    artifact_type="support-reply",
    request_ids=["req_123"],  # the gateway requests that produced it
    claims=[
        {
            "key": "resolves-ticket",
            "claim_type": "resolution",
            "resolves_by": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z",
        }
    ],
)
print(artifact.id, artifact.key, artifact.current_version)

again = client.artifacts.get(artifact.id)
page = client.artifacts.list(limit=20, archetype="draft")
print(len(page.data), page.next_cursor)
```

Lists are cursor-paginated: pass `page.next_cursor` back as `cursor=` for the next page.

A simpler way to bind requests to an artifact is to send `ur={"artifact": "<key>"}` on the
chat call; the response's `ur.artifact_id` echoes the bound artifact.

## Recording outcomes

`client.outcomes.record(target, event)` goes through a durable local queue:

1. the event is finalized: `observed_at` and a client-generated `source_event_id` are fixed;
2. it is persisted to the queue's store;
3. it is sent. If the delivery fails, or its result is unknown, the event stays queued;
   `flush()` replays the identical bytes with the same `Idempotency-Key`, so a delivery the server
   already saw counts as a `duplicate`, never a second event.

`record(...)` never raises for a delivery failure. The receipt's `status` says what happened:

| `status` | When | The event |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `delivered` | the server answered 2xx; `receipt.result` is its per-event verdict | removed from the queue |
| `queued` | everything that does not prove the event was recorded or is invalid: a timeout (including the SDK's own deadline), cancellation, a connection failure, **any** 401, 403, 408 or 429 (whatever the body, code or `retryable` flag), any 5xx, a 4xx without a complete gateway error envelope (an HTML page or an empty body from a proxy, a missing field, `retryable: null` or `"false"`), an unknown or contradictory error code, and a 2xx answer that is not an outcome result (`{}`, `{"data": [{}]}`, an unreadable body) | kept, unchanged, for `flush()`; `receipt.error` says why |
| `rejected` | a validated refusal of the **event**: a 4xx other than 401/403/408/429 whose body is a complete envelope `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id", "retryable": false}}` with `invalid_request` at 400, `not_found` at 404 or `conflict` at 409 | dropped; `receipt.error` says why |

`delivered` needs a result the contract defines: an object whose `status` is `accepted`,
`duplicate`, `conflict` or `rejected` (the server's verdict on the event), or `pending` (an
outcome reported on a request the gateway has not stored yet: the gateway holds a durable receipt
and applies it when the request lands; see
[Plug-and-play learning](learning.md#immediate-outcomes-and-receipts)). These rules are the same
in the TypeScript SDK; both run the same shared fixture of 273 response cases.

To report whether a task succeeded without choosing a channel and kind yourself, use
`client.outcomes.report(request_id, "pass" | "fail" | "unknown", source=...)`: it maps the verdict
through the table both SDKs share, gives the report a stable identity and returns typed receipts.
See [Plug-and-play learning](learning.md#reporting-outcomes).

```python
receipt = client.outcomes.record(artifact.id, {"channel": "behavioral", "kind": "accepted"})
print(receipt.status)  # "delivered", "queued" (will be retried by flush) or "rejected"
print(client.outcomes.size())  # events still waiting in the queue (no network)

# Delayed outcome, attached to a request instead of an artifact:
client.outcomes.record(
    {"request": "req_123"},
    {
        "channel": "resolution",
        "kind": "resolved",
        "value": {"correct": True},
        "claim_key": "resolves-ticket",
    },
)

report = client.outcomes.flush()  # e.g. at shutdown
print(report.delivered, report.rejected, report.pending)
```

| Event field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `channel` (required) | `mechanical`, `correction`, `behavioral`, `resolution`, `computable` or `proxy` |
| `kind` (required) | your event name, for example `accepted`, `edited`, `resolved` |
| `value` | a JSON object with the details |
| `claim_key` / `claim_id` | the claim this event resolves |
| `confidence` | 0..1 |
| `observed_at` | ISO-8601 time; defaults to now |
| `source_event_id` | your idempotency id; generated if omitted |
| `artifact_version`, `alternative_id`, `evidence_hash`, `supersedes_event_id`, `tool_error_class` | optional details |

`client.record_outcome(...)` is an alias of `client.outcomes.record(...)`.

### Durable stores

The default store keeps queued events in memory for the lifetime of the client. To survive
restarts, use a file:

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from ultrarouter import FileOutcomeStore

queue_file = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "outcomes.json"
durable = UltraRouter(outcome_store=FileOutcomeStore(queue_file))
durable.outcomes.record(artifact.id, {"channel": "behavioral", "kind": "accepted"})
durable.outcomes.flush()
```

The file is rewritten atomically with mode `0600`. It starts empty only when it does not exist:
a file that cannot be read, is not valid JSON or does not hold a list of queue entries raises
`OutcomeStoreError` on every operation (including `record` and `flush`) and is never overwritten,
so its events can be recovered by hand. Implement the `OutcomeStore` protocol (`append`,
`update`, `remove`, `list`) to use your own storage.

A client derived with `with_options(...)` shares its parent's store; whichever client delivers an
event uses its own options (see [Clients](clients.md#per-call-settings-and-with_options)).

### Batches and pending claims

```python
batch = client.outcomes.batch(
    [
        {
            "artifact_key": "ticket:4812:reply",
            "channel": "behavioral",
            "kind": "accepted",
            "source_event_id": "evt-1",
        },
        {
            "request_id": "req_123",
            "channel": "proxy",
            "kind": "clicked",
            "source_event_id": "evt-2",
        },
    ]
)
print(batch.accepted, batch.duplicate, batch.conflict, batch.rejected)

pending = client.outcomes.pending(state="overdue", limit=50)
for claim in pending.data:
    print(claim.artifact_key, claim.claim_key, claim.resolves_by)
```

A batch takes up to 1,000 events; each row names its own target. `pending` lists claims that are
waiting for a resolution (cursor-paginated).

## The human-approved final

When a person edits and approves an artifact, record the final version. With the workspace's
corrections consent, you may send the texts; without it, send only statistics and a hash:

```python
from ultrarouter import diff_stats

draft = "Your order will arrive Monday."
final = "Your order will arrive Tuesday, sorry for the delay."
stats = diff_stats(draft, final)
version = client.artifacts.final(artifact.id, diff_stats=stats, final_hash=stats["final_hash"])
print(version.stored, version.client_computed)  # "metadata_only", True
```

See [Diff statistics](diff-stats.md).

## The artifact scope

`with client.with_artifact(key) as scope:` binds chat and embeddings calls to an artifact, records
outcomes on it (creating it on first use) and flushes the queue when the block exits, even on
an exception:

```python
with client.with_artifact("ticket:4813:reply") as scope:
    reply = scope.chat.completions.create(
        model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Draft a reply about a refund."}],
    )
    scope.record({"channel": "behavioral", "kind": "accepted"})
print(scope.artifact_id)
```

The async client's scope is `async with client.with_artifact(key) as scope:` and
`await scope.artifact_id()`.

---

<!-- file: docs/learning.md -->

# Plug-and-play learning

For tools described in prompt text, upload their actual schemas once per call type. Native tool
requests already carry schemas. This replaces the previous set (maximum 256 tools, 1 MiB); an empty
list clears it. Resolve the `ct_…` id with `client.call_types.list()` first.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

with UltraRouter() as client:
    ct = client.call_types.list().data[0]
    client.learning.put_tool_documentation(
        ct.id,
        tools=[
            {
                "type": "function",
                "function": {
                    "name": "set_order_status",
                    "parameters": {
                        "type": "object",
                        "properties": {"status": {"enum": ["reserved", "backordered"]}},
                    },
                },
            }
        ],
    )
    print(client.learning.tool_documentation(ct.id).tool_count)
```

The learning loop turns your agent's traffic plus trustworthy outcomes into candidate adaptations
of a call type, evaluates each candidate against the version serving now (the incumbent), and
promotes it only when the evaluation justifies it. Your part is small:

1. **Correlate**: know each call's request id, and group the steps of one task into an episode.
2. **Report outcomes**: say whether the task succeeded (`pass`, `fail` or `unknown`) and where the
   verdict came from. Report the moment you know, even before the gateway has stored the request.
3. **Control learning**: enable it per call type, pause, resume, inspect versions and evaluations,
   roll back.

A working integration (calls correlated, outcomes accepted) is not evidence that learning helps
your agent: that is decided by the evaluations, against the incumbent, on your own traffic.

Every response is a typed model generated from the API specification (`OutcomeReceiptRecord`,
`LearningStatus`, `LearningControl`, ... in `ultrarouter.types`); unknown fields are kept in
`model_extra`.

## Correlation

Every response carries its request id (`reply.ur.request_id`, and the `x-ur-request-id` header).
You can also mint the id yourself before the call, so you know it even if the answer is lost or
still streaming:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter, new_request_id

client = UltraRouter()
request_id = new_request_id()  # "req_c_" + a ULID; any [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64} works
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}],
    request_id=request_id,  # sent as x-ur-request-id
    episode_key="order:A-100",  # sent as X-UR-Artifact
)
assert reply.ur.request_id == request_id
```

`UltraRouter(request_ids="client")` mints an id for every chat and embeddings call that does not
pass one. When a call fails without an answer (a timeout, a dropped connection), the error's
`request_id` is the id you sent.

A stream knows its request id as soon as it opens, from the response header:

```python
with client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}], stream=True
) as stream:
    print(stream.request_id)  # before the first chunk
    stream.text()
```

**Episodes.** A multi-step task (an agent calling tools) is one episode: every step that carries
the same episode key belongs to it, and one terminal verdict covers all of them. Without a key the
gateway groups steps by their opening text, so **two tasks that open with identical text at the
same time must have distinct keys**, or their steps and verdicts are merged. `new_episode_key()`
mints a unique one; your own stable id (`"order:A-100"`) works too. A key is 1 to 256 printable
ASCII characters without leading or trailing spaces; any other key goes in the body as
`ur.artifact`.

`client.episode(key)` does the bookkeeping: each step gets the key and a freshly minted request
id, and `episode.report(...)` reports on the last step:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
with client.episode("order:A-100") as episode:
    episode.chat.completions.create(
        model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Process order A-100."}]
    )
    # ... more steps: tool calls and their results ...
    report = episode.report("pass", source="verifier")
print(len(episode.request_ids), report.request_id == episode.last_request_id)
```

**With the `openai` package.** Keep your OpenAI client; pass the correlation headers per call and
read the id back with `request_id_of` (it reads the `ur` block the gateway adds, or the header of
a raw response or stream):

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter, correlation_headers, new_request_id, request_id_of

chat = UltraRouter().as_openai()  # or openai.OpenAI(base_url=".../v1", api_key=...)
request_id = new_request_id()
reply = chat.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}],
    extra_headers=correlation_headers(request_id=request_id, episode_key="order:A-100"),
)
assert request_id_of(reply) == request_id
```

## Reporting outcomes

`client.outcomes.report(request_id, verdict, source=...)` maps a verdict to an outcome event
through a table both official SDKs share:

| `source` | `pass` | `fail` | Teaches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `verifier` | `computable` / `oracle_pass` | `computable` / `oracle_fail` | yes |
| `business_rule` | `computable` / `oracle_pass` | `computable` / `oracle_fail` | yes |
| `webhook` | `resolution` / `resolved_true` | `resolution` / `resolved_false` | yes |
| `human_review` | `correction` / `accepted_unchanged` | `correction` / `rejected` | yes |
| `self_rating` | `proxy` / `thumbs` (+1) | `proxy` / `thumbs` (-1) | never |

`verdict="unknown"` sends nothing: missing feedback stays missing. A self-rating is a weak proxy:
it may rank, but it never teaches. The return type says so:

```python
from ultrarouter import (
    NotReportedOutcome,
    ProxyOutcomeReport,
    TeachingOutcomeReport,
    UltraRouter,
)

client = UltraRouter()
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}]
)
request_id = reply.ur.request_id

checked = client.outcomes.report(request_id, "pass", source="verifier")
assert isinstance(checked, TeachingOutcomeReport) and checked.teaches
print(checked.channel, checked.kind, checked.outcome_status)  # computable oracle_pass pending

liked = client.outcomes.report(request_id, "pass", source="self_rating")
assert isinstance(liked, ProxyOutcomeReport) and not liked.teaches

silent = client.outcomes.report(request_id, "unknown", source="verifier")
assert isinstance(silent, NotReportedOutcome) and silent.status == "not_reported"
```

Optional arguments: `idempotency_key` (distinguishes two genuinely different reports with the
same verdict and source, for example a webhook's event id), `observed_at` (ISO-8601 or a
`datetime`; default: the first time the report is made), `evidence_hash` (a hash of the evidence,
never the evidence) and `supersedes` (the `source_event_id` of an earlier report this one revises).

**Never counted twice.** Each report has a stable identity: its `source_event_id` is
`"rpt_" + sha256("ur-outcome-report/v1\n" + request_id + "\n" + verdict + "\n" + source + "\n" +
(idempotency_key or ""))` (`report_source_event_id`), and it travels through the durable outcome
queue under that identity with a matching `Idempotency-Key`. So:

- a lost acknowledgement is retried with the identical event, which the gateway answers as a
  `duplicate`;
- calling `report` again with the same arguments replays the identical bytes (same
  `observed_at`); concurrent repeats share one send;
- a delivery whose outcome is unknown stays queued (`report.status == "queued"`) for
  `client.outcomes.flush()`;
- the same identity with a different payload is sent as its own entry and refused as a conflict,
  never silently replacing the first.

A report repeated from another process derives the same identity; pass `observed_at` explicitly
when that can happen, so the replay is byte-identical.

```python
first = client.outcomes.report(request_id, "fail", source="human_review", idempotency_key="r-1")
again = client.outcomes.report(request_id, "fail", source="human_review", idempotency_key="r-1")
assert again.source_event_id == first.source_event_id
print(again.outcome_status)  # duplicate
```

## Immediate outcomes and receipts

The gateway records requests asynchronously. An outcome reported before that write lands is
accepted at once with `status: "pending"` and a durable receipt (`ocr_...`), then applied when the
request lands, so you never sleep before reporting. Every answer carries the receipt; a retry with
the same identity returns the same receipt. A receipt moves from `pending` to `applied` (with
`outcome_status` `accepted` or `duplicate`), `rejected` (see `reason`), `failed` (recording kept
hitting an internal error) or `expired` (no such request appeared in your workspace within 15
minutes: `reason` is `request_not_found`). Its `episode` says how an applied teaching outcome
relates to the request's episode: `status` is `associated`, `pending`, `not_recorded` or
`not_applicable`, with the episode's `trace_id` and what the outcome did to its `verdict`
(`recorded`, `kept_earlier`, `revised`, `revised_after_incorporation`).

The report call itself can be refused: a gateway-minted id too old to still be in flight is a 404
(the report comes back `rejected`); the same identity with a different payload is a 409; when the
workspace already holds 5,000 pending receipts the gateway answers 429 `outcome_backlog_full`
(`OutcomeBacklogFullError`) with `Retry-After`, which the SDK honours, and the report stays queued.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say OK."}]
)
report = client.outcomes.report(reply.ur.request_id, "pass", source="verifier")
print(report.is_pending, report.receipt_id)

final = client.outcomes.wait_for_receipt(report, timeout=30)  # bounded backoff polling
print(final.status, final.outcome_status, final.episode.status)

for receipt in client.outcomes.receipts_for_request(reply.ur.request_id).data:
    print(receipt.id, receipt.status)
```

`wait_for_receipt` reads the public receipt endpoint with a doubling interval (0.25 s up to 4 s by
default) for at most `timeout` seconds, retrying transient read failures; on the deadline it raises
`ReceiptWaitTimeoutError` with `receipt_id` and `last_receipt`. The outcome is not lost: the
receipt keeps reconciling on the gateway. On `AsyncUltraRouter` the wait is cancellable:

```python
import asyncio

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncUltraRouter() as client:
        reply = await client.chat.completions.create(
            model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say OK."}]
        )
        report = await client.outcomes.report(reply.ur.request_id, "pass", source="verifier")
        waiting = asyncio.ensure_future(client.outcomes.wait_for_receipt(report))
        waiting.cancel()  # stops at once; the outcome is unaffected
        final = await asyncio.wait_for(client.outcomes.wait_for_receipt(report), timeout=35)
        print(final.status)


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Outcome adapters

`ultrarouter.adapters` turns checks you already have into verdicts, with the same semantics,
reasons and hashes as the TypeScript SDK's `@ultrarouter/sdk/learning` entry. A check that cannot
decide (it crashed, timed out, the process was killed) is `unknown`, never a `fail`. Reasons and
outputs stay local; only the verdict, its source and an optional evidence hash are sent.
`evidence_hash(value)` is `"sha256:"` plus the hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the evidence
(keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8).

**A computable check, a command or a test suite** (`source="verifier"`):

```python
import sys

from ultrarouter.adapters import run_test_suite, run_verifier, verdict_from_command

answer = 42
check = run_verifier(lambda: answer == 17 + 25)
print(check.verdict)  # pass

detailed = run_verifier(lambda: {"pass": answer == 41, "evidence": {"answer": answer}})
print(detailed.verdict, detailed.evidence_hash)  # fail sha256:...

suite = run_test_suite([sys.executable, "-c", "raise SystemExit(0)"])  # e.g. ["pytest", "-q"]
print(suite.verdict)  # pass; exit code 1 would be ('fail', ('exit_code_1',))

print(verdict_from_command(None, signal_name="SIGKILL").verdict)  # unknown
```

A check returns `True` / `False`, or `{"pass": bool, "evidence": ..., "reasons": [...]}`. One that
raises is `unknown` (`verifier_error`) unless `on_error="fail"`; a failing `assert` is always a
`fail` (`check_threw`). A command passes on exit code 0 and fails on any other (list "could not
decide" codes in `unknown_codes`, such as pytest's 5).

**Structured output and business rules** (`source="business_rule"`), with pydantic. A validator
always decides, so the verdict is `pass` or `fail`:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

from ultrarouter.adapters import validate_output


class Refund(BaseModel):
    order_id: str
    amount: float


result = validate_output(
    '{"order_id": "A-100", "amount": -5}',
    Refund,
    rules={
        "amount is positive": lambda refund: refund.amount > 0,
        "known order": lambda refund: True if refund.order_id.startswith("A-") else "unknown order",
    },
)
print(result.verdict, result.reasons)  # fail ('amount is positive',)
```

Output that is not JSON fails with `invalid_json`; a field problem gives `"$.<field>: <message>"`;
a rule returning `False` gives its name, a rule returning a string `"<name>: <string>"`, a rule that
raises `"<name>: <exception class>"`. Reasons never quote the output's values. Report either
result with `client.outcomes.report(request_id, result.verdict, source=result.source,
evidence_hash=result.evidence_hash)`.

**A signed, delayed webhook** (`source="webhook"`). When a business system learns the outcome later
(a refund settled, a ticket reopened), it calls your webhook route. The sender signs
`"<timestamp>.<raw body>"` with HMAC-SHA256 under a shared secret and sends
`x-webhook-signature: sha256=<hex>` and `x-webhook-timestamp` (Unix seconds); `sign_webhook`
builds them. `WebhookOutcomeHandler` checks, in order: both headers present and well formed, the
timestamp within ±300 s, the signature in constant time (`hmac.compare_digest`; several secrets
are accepted for rotation), then the payload (`event_id`, `request_id`, `verdict`, optional
`observed_at` and `evidence_hash`). It claims the `event_id` in a `DedupeStore` (in memory by
default, held 7 days; back it with a unique database row to share it across processes) and
reports once, with the event id as the `idempotency_key`. The secret comes from
`ULTRAROUTER_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (or `secret=`) and is never logged.

```python
import json
import time

from ultrarouter import UltraRouter
from ultrarouter.adapters import WebhookOutcomeHandler, WebhookVerifier, sign_webhook

secret = "demo-only-secret"  # in production: WebhookVerifier() reads ULTRAROUTER_WEBHOOK_SECRET
handler = WebhookOutcomeHandler(WebhookVerifier(secret))
client = UltraRouter()

# What the business system sends:
body = json.dumps({"event_id": "evt_42", "request_id": "req_c_example", "verdict": "fail"})
headers = sign_webhook(body, secret=secret, now_s=time.time())

first = handler.handle(client, body, headers)
print(first.status, first.http_status)  # reported 200
again = handler.handle(client, body, headers)
print(again.status, again.http_status)  # duplicate 200: a redelivery is a no-op
```

Answer the sender with `result.http_status`:

| `status` | `http_status` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reported` | 200 | reported with `source="webhook"` (an `unknown` verdict reports nothing) |
| `duplicate` | 200 | this event id was already handled |
| `rejected` | 401 / 400 | refused before anything was reported; `reason` is `missing_signature`, `missing_timestamp`, `malformed_signature`, `malformed_timestamp`, `stale_timestamp`, `bad_signature` or `malformed_payload` (400) |
| `deferred` | 503 | the gateway has not acknowledged the report yet; the claim was released so the sender's redelivery reports again, under the same identity |

When the payload has no `observed_at`, the signed timestamp is used, so processes racing on one
delivery send byte-identical events. Use `ahandle` with `AsyncUltraRouter`, and `parse=` for
another payload shape; `WebhookVerifier.verify(body, headers)` alone raises a
`WebhookVerificationError` subclass (with `reason`) for a refused delivery.

## Learning controls

`client.learning` steers learning for one call type at a time (reads need `config:read`, controls
`config:write`; manual promote and reject need an owner or admin). Every control returns a
`LearningControl`: the `action`, whether it `changed` anything (controls are idempotent), the
version it acted on, an evaluation it stopped, and the resulting `learning` status.

Before enabling learning, an owner or admin must grant the workspace's full self-learning
opt-in: **knowledge and corrections consent**. Use the dashboard Learning page or a signed-in
session calling `PUT /v1/workspaces/{id}/self-learning` with `{"enabled":true}`. An API key
cannot grant consent, and corrections consent alone is insufficient. The reflection model must
resolve to a workspace-owned provider; learning has no platform or paid fallback.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
learning = client.learning
call_type = next((ct for ct in client.call_types.list().data if ct.slug == "support-reply"), None)
if call_type is None:
    call_type = client.call_types.create(slug="support-reply")
call_type_id = call_type.id  # learning endpoints require the ct_… id, not the slug

control = learning.enable(
    call_type_id,
    reflection_model="openai/gpt-5.2-mini",  # must resolve to a workspace-owned offer
    promotion={"mode": "evaluate", "objective": "success", "min_verified_per_arm": 30},
    recipe={"validator": "elv2", "generation": "atomic", "observations": "elo2"},
)
status = control.learning
print(status.state, status.reason, status.active_version.id if status.active_version else None)

learning.pause(call_type_id)  # stop reflecting and deciding; the active version keeps serving
learning.resume(call_type_id)

for version in learning.versions(call_type_id).data:
    print(version.id, version.version, version.state)
detail = learning.version(call_type_id, "epb_3")  # lessons, reflection receipt, transitions
for evaluation in learning.evaluations(call_type_id).data:
    print(evaluation.id, evaluation.decision, evaluation.arms.candidate.verified)

learning.promote(call_type_id, "epb_3")  # an owner/admin decision; a running evaluation stops
learning.rollback(call_type_id, version_id="epb_1")  # point the active version at an earlier one
learning.disable(call_type_id)  # stop serving learned lessons (the kill switch)
```

`status(...)` reports the `state` with a `reason`: `off`, `collecting` (enabled, waiting for
evidence), `learning` (a reflection is due or an evaluation runs), `paused`, `disabled`,
`unavailable` (no workspace-owned reflection provider; `reflection.provider.reason` says why),
`quota_exhausted` or `budget_exhausted`; a stopped learner always says why. It also carries the
active version and the latest candidate, the running and the latest evaluation (frozen rule,
arms, the interval on the difference, the decision), the promotion policy, the learner recipe,
the `evidence` (recorded, verified pass / fail, unknown, consumed, incorporated by the active
version, backlog), the `outcome_receipts` by state, the `budget` and the subscription `usage`
(recorded apart from cash). With promotion mode `evaluate` a candidate becomes active only by
winning a prospective randomized evaluation against the incumbent; every other decision keeps
the incumbent.

The gateway names each refusal with a code at the start of its message
(`corrections_consent_required: ...`, `promotion_invalid (alpha_range)`). The SDK raises an
actionable `LearningError` subclass (the TypeScript SDK's vocabulary) whose `reason` names the
problem, `refusal` the gateway's named refusal (else the error code), `detail` the sub-reason in
parentheses, and `action` (also appended to the message) what to do:

| Exception | `reason` | Gateway refusal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LearningConsentRequiredError` | `missing_consent` | 409 `corrections_consent_required` |
| `LearningProviderUnavailableError` | `provider_unavailable` | 400 `reflection_model_not_workspace_owned (<detail>)`: `no_offer`, `platform_offer_only`, `no_workspace_key`, `model_denied_by_policy`, `workspace_funding_not_byok` or `workspace_funding_frozen` |
| `LearningPolicyInvalidError` | `invalid_promotion` | 400 `promotion_invalid (<field>)` |
| `LearningNotEnabledError` | `not_enabled` | 409 `learning_not_enabled` |
| `LearningVersionConflictError` | `version_conflict` | 409 `version_already_active` (promote), `version_active` (reject: roll back instead), `no_rollback_target` / `rollback_target_not_earlier` (rollback) |
| `LearningQuotaExhaustedError` | `quota_exhausted` | the learning provider refused for quota |
| `LearningBudgetExhaustedError` | `budget_exhausted` | the learning budget is spent |
| `LearningNotFoundError` (also a `NotFoundError`) | `not_found` | 404 `not_found`: unknown call type or version |
| `LearningForbiddenError` (also a `PermissionDeniedError`) | `forbidden` | 403 `permission`: the key lacks the scope |

```python
from ultrarouter import LearningError, UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
try:
    client.learning.status("ct_missing")
except LearningError as exc:
    print(exc.reason, "->", exc.action)
```

`client.call_types.episode_memory` (`get`, `enable`, `disable`) reads and switches the lower-level
episode-memory setting learning writes; `enable` there is a lab-authorised lever, so use
`client.learning.enable` for learning.

## A demonstration environment

`ultrarouter.demo.OrderDesk` is a small, deterministic tool environment (an order desk with
stock, orders and four tools) whose exact rules and verifier come from a fixture shared byte for
byte with the TypeScript SDK; tool results, verifier reasons and evidence hashes are identical in
both. It exists to show the loop working end to end; **it is a demonstration, not evidence that
learning improves an agent**.

```python
from ultrarouter.demo import NOTICE, OrderDesk

desk = OrderDesk("s3")  # "Process orders C-300 and C-301." with 4 units for 6 ordered
print(desk.task, [tool["function"]["name"] for tool in desk.tools])
print(
    desk.call("check_stock", {"sku": "SKU-GREEN"})
)  # {'ok': True, 'sku': 'SKU-GREEN', 'in_stock': 4}
print(desk.verify().verdict)  # fail: nothing done yet
desk.solve()  # the deterministic reference procedure, no model
print(desk.verify().verdict)  # pass
print(NOTICE)
```

The tools answer `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` with `UNKNOWN_ORDER`, `UNKNOWN_SKU`,
`SKU_MISMATCH`, `ALREADY_RESERVED`, `INSUFFICIENT_STOCK` (with `in_stock`), `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`
or `UNKNOWN_TOOL`, and an error changes nothing. As in JSON Schema, `"quantity": 2.0` is the
integer 2, while `2.5`, `true` and `"2"` are `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`. The verifier handles orders in the order the
task names them: each must end `reserved` with its full quantity if the stock left covered it,
otherwise `backordered` with nothing reserved, and each SKU's final stock must equal its starting
stock minus what was reserved for it.

Hand `desk.tools` to `chat.completions.create(tools=...)`, run each tool call with
`desk.tool_message(call)`, then report `desk.verify()` on the episode's last step; see
`examples/learning_tool_episode.py`.

## Examples

Runnable scripts (each takes `ULTRAROUTER_API_KEY` and `ULTRAROUTER_BASE_URL`, prints a short
result and exits non-zero on failure):

| Script | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| [`learning_openai_client.py`](../examples/learning_openai_client.py) | the `openai` package unchanged, plus a minted request id and an outcome report |
| [`learning_native_verifier.py`](../examples/learning_native_verifier.py) | the native SDK with a real, computable verifier |
| [`learning_tool_episode.py`](../examples/learning_tool_episode.py) | a multi-step tool episode, correlated, with one terminal verdict |
| [`learning_immediate_outcome.py`](../examples/learning_immediate_outcome.py) | reporting at once (pending receipt), then following the receipt |
| [`learning_delayed_webhook.py`](../examples/learning_delayed_webhook.py) | a signed delayed webhook: deduplicated, refused when forged or stale |
| [`learning_ack_loss.py`](../examples/learning_ack_loss.py) | a lost acknowledgement and a repeated report, recorded once |
| [`learning_controls.py`](../examples/learning_controls.py) | enable, pause, resume, versions, evaluations, rollback, typed errors |
| [`learning_async.py`](../examples/learning_async.py) | the async client, with a cancellable receipt wait |

<!-- file: docs/imports.md -->

# History imports

Imports bring existing usage data or traces into the ledger without routing traffic through the
gateway: an exported usage report gives the gateway a spend and model picture from day one;
intact traces (with prompts and outputs, under the workspace's consent) can also feed evals.

An import never invents data it was not given: a usage-only export cannot create prompts,
outputs or quality figures. Imports need a key with `outcomes:write`.

## Preview, then commit

`mode="preview"` parses and reports without storing anything:

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
records = [
    {"model": "gpt-5.2-mini", "input_tokens": 1200, "output_tokens": 300, "date": "2026-01-10"},
    {"model": "gpt-5.2", "input_tokens": 800, "output_tokens": 500, "date": "2026-01-10"},
]

preview = client.imports.create(format="openai_usage", records=records, mode="preview")
print(preview.status, preview.import_class, preview.record_count)
print(preview.report.unsupported_fields, preview.report.parse_errors)

committed = client.imports.create(format="openai_usage", records=records, mode="commit")
print(committed.id, committed.status, committed.accepted_count, committed.rejected_count)
```

Pass the raw export as JSON Lines text with `jsonl=` instead of `records=`. `call_type_id=` binds
the imported history to a call type; `import_id=` resumes an earlier import.

## Track and cancel

```python
job = client.imports.get(committed.id)
print(job.status)  # preview, running, completed, cancelled or failed

for item in client.imports.list(limit=10).data:
    print(item.id, item.format, item.status)

if job.status == "running":
    client.imports.cancel(job.id)
```

The `format` names the source adapter for your export; the import's `report` lists anything it
could not use (`unsupported_fields`, `parse_errors`, per-reason counts).

---

<!-- file: docs/flywheel.md -->

# Flywheel

The flywheel turns your recorded outcomes into improvement candidates (learned context, model
changes, hosted-prompt drafts), screens them offline, confirms them on live traffic against a
holdout, and lets a person adopt them. This page covers the read and decision surfaces; most
reads need `config:read`, writes need `outcomes:write`.

## Status

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
status = client.flywheel.status()
print(status.usage.tracked_artifacts, status.usage.accepted_outcomes)
for channel in status.channels:
    print(channel.channel, channel.accepted_outcomes, channel.last_observed_at)
print(status.imports.total, status.learning.flywheel_class)

learning = client.flywheel.calibration()  # the same read's `learning` block
print(learning.calibration_available, learning.flywheel_class_reason)
```

`calibration()` reports whether calibration is available; it never fabricates a track record.

## Improvement reads

For every call type, two reads side by side: can it spend less (a cheaper model is enough) and can
it get better (a quality improvement is available). Each half is one state with the next action.

```python
reads = client.improvement_reads.list()
for row in reads.call_types:
    print(row.slug, row.spend_less.state, row.get_better.state, row.get_better.next_action)
```

States are `evidence`, `collecting`, `needs_confirmation`, `keep_incumbent` and `unavailable`.
An `evidence` read names its evidence tier and is labelled when it is an estimate.

## What to do next

```python
plan = client.flywheel.moat_next(lever_family="learned_context")
for item in plan.items:
    print(item.call_type_id, item.situation_class, item.ready, item.next_action)
```

## Exposure grants

A grant assigns one call to the treated or holdout arm of a live experiment, so improvement can be
measured even when you call providers directly. [Preflight](preflight.md) returns the grant for you;
mint one directly with:

```python
grant = client.flywheel.grant(artifact_key="ticket:4812:reply", call_type="support-reply")
print(grant.grant_id, grant.arm, grant.epoch, grant.valid_until_epoch_close)
```

The same key in the same epoch always yields the same grant. Pass either `artifact_key` or
`trace_id`.

## Candidates, confirmations and decisions

```python
candidates = client.flywheel.candidates.list()
for candidate in candidates.candidates:
    print(candidate.run_id, candidate.lever_key, candidate.offline_verdict, candidate.live_verdict)

confirmations = client.flywheel.confirmations()
for confirmation in confirmations.confirmations:
    print(
        confirmation.candidate_ref,
        confirmation.status,
        confirmation.result_outcome,
        confirmation.adoptable,
    )

state = client.flywheel.candidates.confirmation("cand_ref_1")
print(state.present, state.adoptable, state.adopt_refusal)
```

A person records accept / reject / revert decisions. The request is signed with your API key and
replay-safe (re-sending the same decision returns `duplicate`); the decision is an audit record,
never a learning label:

```python
decision = client.flywheel.candidates.decide(
    "cand_ref_1",
    decision="accept",
    actor_id="alice@example.com",
    reason="Screening and live confirmation both reviewed.",
    evidence_hash="0" * 64,
    workspace_id="ws_123",
)
print(decision.status, decision.callback_id)
```

A CI system can ask whether a screened candidate's controlled rollout is unlocked; the server
decides and names every blocker, and never starts the rollout itself:

```python
rollout = client.flywheel.candidates.rollout(
    "cand_ref_1",
    candidate_state="screened",
    change_shape="gateway_owned",
    observed_identity={
        "repository": "acme/app",
        "workflowId": "support-reply",
        "baseSha": "a1b2c3",
        "headSha": "d4e5f6",
        "configHash": "cfg-1",
        "datasetSplit": "holdout",
        "evaluatorVersion": "ev-1",
        "evidenceEpoch": "1",
        "harnessHash": "h-1",
        "lockDigest": "l-1",
        "objective": "acceptance_rate",
    },
    requires_repository_write=False,
)
print(rollout.unlocked, [b.reason for b in rollout.blockers], rollout.pressed)
```

## Running a bounded experiment

A bounded experiment is a preregistered, candidate-frozen comparison a workspace owner sets up: a
fixed set of idea families (pairs), each with two slots the gateway assigns to opposite arms
(`control` and `treated`). A runner — a key with the `flywheel:experiment:run` scope (never implied
by `gateway:invoke`) — drives each execution with `client.flywheel.experiments`. Enrol an execution
before its first call, send the returned `execution_id` as the `EXPERIMENT_EXECUTION_HEADER` header
on every call of the run (each with a fresh trace attempt), then dry-run and record the one terminal
outcome and ask for the evaluation. The gateway decides the arm, never the caller; a repeat of the
same `{phase, pair_key, slot}` returns the same execution, so a resume re-enrols the identical tuple
safely — never change the slot to work around a failure.

```python
from ultrarouter import EXPERIMENT_EXECUTION_HEADER

execution = client.flywheel.experiments.enrol("fxp_1", phase="screen", pair_key="idea-a", slot=0)
# Carry this header on every call of the execution (POST /v1/messages, POST /v1/responses):
call_headers = {EXPERIMENT_EXECUTION_HEADER: execution.execution_id}
print(execution.arm, execution.created, call_headers)

outcome_fields = dict(
    terminal="delivered",
    reason_codes=[],
    reason_vocab="ur.experiment.reasons.v1",
    receipts=[
        {
            "ordinal": 0,
            "stage": "writer",
            "call_type": "support-reply",
            "request_id": "req_...",
            "extractor_version": "ex.v1",
            "numbers": {"post_length": 280},
        }
    ],
    final_content_hash="0" * 64,
    request_ids=["req_..."],
)

# Dry-run first: the same validation, nothing written. The dry-run shape carries `refusal`.
dry = client.flywheel.experiments.outcome(
    "fxp_1", execution.execution_id, dry_run=True, **outcome_fields
)
print(dry.object, dry.status, dry.refusal, dry.recorded_outcome)
if dry.status != "refused":
    recorded = client.flywheel.experiments.outcome(
        "fxp_1", execution.execution_id, **outcome_fields
    )
    print(recorded.object, recorded.status)

# Re-evaluate the screen (idempotent; the verdict is computed once, only at the barrier).
screen = client.flywheel.experiments.evaluate_screen("fxp_1")
print(screen.object, screen.computed, screen.experiment_state)
```

Named refusals reach you on the typed error: branch on `exc.code` and read the specific reason
(`experiment_not_live`, `phase_not_open`, `phase_unfunded`, `pair_not_in_manifest`,
`outcome_conflict`, `receipt_missing:<stage>`, `membership_incomplete`, …) in `exc.message`. The same
reasons come back on an outcome dry run as its `refusal`, so you can see what recording would do
before writing anything. The owner-session parts (funding a phase, holds and reconciliation,
judgements, acknowledgement) are not on an API key and are not part of this resource.

## Learning plans and prompt candidates

```python
for proposal in client.flywheel.plans().plans:
    print(proposal.id, proposal.workflow_id, proposal.review_state, proposal.provenance)

envelope = client.flywheel.plan("support-reply")  # plan is None while still collecting
print(envelope.workflow_id, envelope.plan.review_state if envelope.plan else "collecting")

for draft in client.flywheel.prompt_candidates().candidates:
    print(draft.version_id, draft.status, draft.is_active_version, draft.approve_refusal)
```

Related: [Oracles and verdict sources](oracles.md), [Reviewer adapter](reviewer.md),
[Preflight and learned context](preflight.md).

<!-- file: docs/oracles.md -->

# Oracles and verdict sources

An *oracle* is a check you own that can tell a right answer from a wrong one (a label set, schema
rules, a test endpoint, a reconciliation job, or your CI). Registered checks earn a role
(`detector` or `certifier`) by being qualified against planted failures; only qualified checks
count. A *verdict source* is anything that reports task outcomes; it must show it reports known
failures as failures before its verdicts count toward readiness.

## Register a check

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
registration = client.flywheel.oracles.register(
    kind="customer_ci",
    transport="pull",
    spec={"description": "Runs the order-status contract tests"},
)
print(registration.oracle_id, registration.version_hash, registration.inserted)
secret = registration.secret  # pull / push only: returned once, store it securely
```

`kind` is `label_set`, `schema_rules`, `test_endpoint`, `reconciliation` or `customer_ci`;
`transport` is `platform` (runs inside the gateway), `push` (the gateway calls your endpoint) or
`pull` (your worker claims jobs). Registering the same spec again is a no-op; a changed spec
appends a version.

```python
oracle = client.flywheel.oracles.get(registration.oracle_id)
print(
    oracle.revoked,
    oracle.role.qualified,
    oracle.role.reason,
    [v.version_hash for v in oracle.versions],
)
```

## Qualify and test

```python
qualification = client.flywheel.oracles.qualify(
    registration.oracle_id,
    examples=[{"input": f"order {n} status?", "output": f"Order {n} shipped."} for n in range(10)],
)
print(qualification.status, qualification.result, qualification.role)

probe = client.flywheel.oracles.test(registration.oracle_id, probe={"input": "q", "output": "a"})
print(probe.status, probe.verdict)
```

Qualification plants failures into your known-good examples; a pull check's probes wait for your
worker (`status="pending"`) and are graded when the last verdict arrives.

## Pull transport: claim jobs and post verdicts

A pull worker claims due jobs and answers each with `pass` or `fail`. Both calls are signed with
the oracle secret (`X-UR-Oracle-Signature`); the SDK signs the exact bytes it sends.

```python
jobs = client.flywheel.oracles.claim_jobs(registration.oracle_id, secret=secret or "", max=10)
verdicts = []
for job in jobs.data:
    passed = job.output.strip() != ""  # your real check goes here
    verdicts.append(
        {
            "job_id": job.job_id,
            "oracle_version": job.oracle_version,
            "candidate_sha256": job.candidate_sha256,
            "verdict": "pass" if passed else "fail",
            **({} if passed else {"reasons": ["missing_field"]}),
        }
    )
if verdicts:
    result = client.flywheel.oracles.submit_verdicts(
        registration.oracle_id, secret=secret or "", verdicts=verdicts
    )
    print(result.accepted, result.duplicate, result.refused)
```

Each job payload is returned once. Posting the same verdict again is a visible `duplicate`; a
different answer for an answered job is a `conflict` and never overwrites.

## Revoke

```python
revocation = client.flywheel.oracles.revoke(registration.oracle_id)
print(revocation.already_revoked, revocation.cancelled_jobs)
```

Revocation is terminal: every receipt of every version stops counting.

## Verdict sources

```python
sources = client.flywheel.sources()
for source in sources.data:
    print(source.verdict_source, source.eligible, source.reason, source.eligible_task_verdicts)
```

To qualify a source, issue a planted-failure check and answer every probe exactly once with
`resolved_true` or `resolved_false`:

```python
check = client.flywheel.source_checks.issue(call_type_id="ct_123")
answers = [{"probe_id": probe.probe_id, "kind": "resolved_false"} for probe in check.probes]
graded = client.flywheel.source_checks.grade(check.id, verdicts=answers)
print(graded.result, graded.qualified, graded.recall.value, graded.specificity.value)
```

Only the credential that issued a check can answer it, and a check is graded once.

<!-- file: docs/reviewer.md -->

# Reviewer adapter

`client.reviewer` sends your reviewers' decisions (approved, approved with edits, rejected,
regenerated) into the outcome ledger. It is the contract your review tool posts to; no
third-party connectors are included.

Properties you can rely on:

- **Signed.** Every delivery is signed with your API key: `HMAC-SHA256` over
  `"<unix-seconds>.<exact body>"`, sent as `X-UR-Reviewer-Signature: sha256=<hex>` with
  `X-UR-Reviewer-Timestamp`. The SDK serializes the body once and signs those bytes.
- **Durable.** `record()` persists an event locally without touching the network; `flush()`
  sends queued events in signed batches. Only a valid per-event verdict moves an event: one with
  the event's `event_id` as a string and `status` `accepted` or `duplicate` (removed), or
  `rejected` / `unsupported` with a string `reason` and a boolean `repairable` (dropped when
  `false`, kept as a dead letter when `true`). Anything else (a non-string `event_id`, an unknown
  status, a missing reason, a `data` that is not a list) keeps the event queued. `flush()` never
  raises on a 2xx answer. A failed batch always stays queued: an ambiguous failure (timeout,
  connection failure, 408/429/5xx) ends the flush quietly (`report.pending`), and any other
  non-retryable 4xx (for example an invalid signature) is raised.
- **Nothing lost.** A refusal the server marks *repairable* (for example a version mismatch) is
  kept as a local dead letter so you can `repair()` it; terminal refusals are dropped.
- **Provenance is the server's.** The event shape has no field for source or learning use.

Requires a key with `outcomes:write`.

## Guided setup

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
setup = client.reviewer.setup()
print(setup.endpoint, setup.required_scope)
print(setup.signature.header, setup.signature.algorithm, setup.signature.tolerance_seconds)
for row in setup.mapping:
    print(row.decision, "->", row.channel, row.kind)

result = client.reviewer.test("happy")  # also "replay" and "version_mismatch"
print(result.scenario, result.result.status, result.excluded_from_learning)
```

Test scenarios never enter learning or billing.

## Record and flush

```python
event = {
    "event_id": "review-7781",  # your stable id: re-sending it is a no-op
    "artifact_key": "ticket:4812:reply",  # or "artifact_id"
    "artifact_version": 1,
    "decision": "approved_with_edits",
    "effective_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00Z",
    "reviewer_id": "agent-42",
}
client.reviewer.record(event, reviewer_system="helpdesk")
report = client.reviewer.flush()
print(report.accepted, report.duplicate, report.dead_lettered, report.dropped, report.pending)
```

To send immediately instead of queueing, use `send()` (at most 500 events per call):

```python
response = client.reviewer.send([{**event, "event_id": "review-7782"}], reviewer_system="helpdesk")
print(response.accepted, [row.status for row in response.data])
```

A declared backfill reports progress per id: `record(event, backfill={"id": "import-2026-01",
"total": 1200})`, then `{"id": ..., "complete": True}` on the last batch.

## Including the final text or its statistics

With the workspace's corrections consent you may include the approved text; without it, send
only statistics and a hash:

```python
from ultrarouter import diff_stats

stats = diff_stats("Draft reply.", "Final reply, with edits.")
client.reviewer.record(
    {
        **event,
        "event_id": "review-7783",
        "final": {"diff_stats": stats, "hash": stats["final_hash"]},
    }
)
client.reviewer.flush()
```

## Dead letters and repair

```python
for letter in client.reviewer.dead_letters():
    print(letter["event"]["event_id"], letter["dead_letter"]["reason"])
    repaired = client.reviewer.repair(letter, repin_to_current_version=True)
    print(repaired.before.reason, repaired.result.status if repaired.result else None)

health = client.reviewer.health()
print(health.events.accepted, health.dead_letter_total, health.next_repair.action)
```

A successful repair removes the local dead letter. `health()` names the next repair action.

## Verifying signatures in your own tooling

The signing helpers are exported, so a non-Python reviewer system can be checked against this
implementation:

```python
from ultrarouter import reviewer_signature_headers, sign_payload

body = b'{"events":[]}'
print(sign_payload("ur_sk_test_example", "1760000000", body))
print(reviewer_signature_headers("ur_sk_test_example", body, now_s=1760000000))
```

Durable storage across restarts works as for outcomes: pass
`reviewer_store=FileOutcomeStore(path)` to the client.

<!-- file: docs/preflight.md -->

# Preflight and learned context

Preflight is for calls you make **yourself**, directly to a model provider, while still using
what the gateway knows. Before the call, `client.preflight(...)` (`POST /v1/preflight`) answers:

- which model to use and the health-ordered fallbacks;
- which learned context module to inject, and where;
- the active hosted prompt, if the call type has one;
- with a cluster key (`artifact_key` or `trace_id`), the **exposure grant** that puts this call
  in the treated or holdout arm of a live experiment.

Preflight never calls a model and is never charged as one. It needs a key with
`gateway:invoke`.

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

client = UltraRouter()
advice = client.preflight(call_type="support-reply", artifact_key="ticket:4812:reply")

print(advice.routing.mode, advice.routing.model.id if advice.routing.model else None)
print([fallback.id for fallback in advice.routing.fallbacks])
if advice.knowledge is not None:
    print(advice.knowledge.placement, advice.knowledge.module.tokens)
else:
    print("no learned module:", advice.knowledge_reason)
print(advice.grant.arm if advice.grant else advice.grant_reason)
print(advice.provisional, advice.reason)
```

## `messages` for case-based modules

Some call types (classification tasks in particular) learn *verified cases* instead of a fixed
module: the module is rendered for the input of each request, from the cases nearest to it. For
those, pass the messages you are about to send. Without them, preflight returns
`knowledge=None` with `knowledge_reason="case_query_missing"`.

```python
messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "Classify the ticket."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "I was charged twice for my subscription."},
]

without = client.preflight(call_type="ticket-classifier")
print(without.knowledge, without.knowledge_reason)  # None case_query_missing

advice = client.preflight(call_type="ticket-classifier", messages=messages)
print(advice.knowledge.module.content if advice.knowledge else advice.knowledge_reason)
```

The messages are used only to render the module; the gateway does not store or log them, and the
SDK's cache keys on a digest of them (never the text), so a module rendered for one input is
never reused for another. A static (non-case) module ignores `messages`.

## `use_learned`: preflight plus placement plus outcomes

`client.use_learned(...)` preflights once and returns a
[`LearnedSession`](api-reference.md#learnedsession):

- `session.apply(messages)` returns your messages with the learned module inserted exactly where
  the gateway would put it (after the leading system messages). For a holdout arm, or when no
  module is configured, it returns the messages unchanged.
- `session.record(outcome)` upserts the artifact (`artifact_key`) with the grant attached, then
  records the outcome through the durable queue.

```python
session = client.use_learned(
    call_type="support-reply",
    artifact_key="ticket:4812:reply",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Where is my refund?"}],
)

prompt_messages = session.apply(
    [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a support agent."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Where is my refund?"},
    ]
)
model = session.model or "openai/gpt-5.2-mini"
# ... call your provider directly with `model` and `prompt_messages` ...

receipt = session.record({"channel": "behavioral", "kind": "accepted"})
print(receipt.status, session.grant.arm if session.grant else None)
```

`apply` always injects the returned module, whatever `knowledge.delivery` says: `delivery`
describes whether the gateway injects on *proxied* requests, and a direct call never passes
through the gateway. `record` requires `artifact_key`; without it, it raises
`InvalidRequestError` instead of silently recording an outcome with no grant.

## Hosted prompts

`advice.prompt` is the active hosted prompt (or `None` for a code-owned call type);
`client.get_prompt(call_type)` returns just that part. Render it with
[`render_prompt`](prompt-render.md).

## Caching

Preflight answers have two lifetimes, and the client honours both:

| Part | Lifetime | How the SDK handles it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config part (model, learned module, hosted prompt) | `Cache-Control: max-age=5` + strong `ETag` | served from cache while fresh; then revalidated with `If-None-Match` (a `304` reuses the cached body) |
| Live part (health-ordered fallbacks) | 30 s (`X-UR-Live-Max-Age`) | after it expires, a full refetch |
| Grant | never cached | read from the `X-UR-Grant` header of every response, including a `304` |

A request with a cluster key always reaches the gateway (to get a fresh grant). Options:

```python
fresh = client.preflight(call_type="support-reply", no_cache=True)  # bypass the cache
short = client.preflight(call_type="support-reply", max_age_s=10)  # shrink the live window
print(fresh.config_version, short.config_version)
```

The cache is bounded. It keeps at most 1024 request identities per client by default
(`DEFAULT_PREFLIGHT_CACHE_SIZE`); storing one more evicts the least recently used, and entries
whose live part has expired are dropped (they could never be served again). A long-lived client
that sends unique `trace_id`, `artifact_key` or `messages` on every call therefore stays within the
bound. Choose the size with `preflight_cache_size=` (`0` turns the cache off):

```python
from ultrarouter import UltraRouter

small = UltraRouter(preflight_cache_size=128)
uncached = UltraRouter(preflight_cache_size=0)
```

A client derived with `with_options(...)` shares its parent's cache. The cache decision is a pure
function, `ultrarouter.decide_preflight_cache`, if you want to reason about it or reuse it.

## Async

```python
import asyncio

from ultrarouter import AsyncUltraRouter


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncUltraRouter() as client:
        advice = await client.preflight(
            call_type="ticket-classifier",
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Refund not received"}],
        )
        session = await client.use_learned(call_type="support-reply", artifact_key="ticket:9")
        print(advice.knowledge_reason, session.apply([{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]))
        await session.record({"channel": "behavioral", "kind": "accepted"})


asyncio.run(main())
```
